title: Wrongful Yearning
author: buxus
synopsis:
Everyone knows that the Seventh Prince, Xiao Cheng, is a good-for-nothing. The nobles of the capital despise him, and the powerful officials at court bully him.
Even the marriage bestowed by the Emperor was a calculated move: he was forced to marry Shen Li, a fierce daughter of a military family with achievements so great they threatened the throne and a temper as explosive as fire. It was called a favor, but it was actually surveillance.
On their wedding night, Shen Li looked at her timid husband with cold eyes, feeling nothing but disdain: "Coward."
She did not know that the sheep she was looking at had long since sharpened its fangs and had even prepared a private army capable of devouring the world.
Xiao Cheng had been biding his time for ten years, waiting only to be sent to his fiefdom so he could return to the sea like a dragon.
He used the Shen family’s influence to stabilize his fief; he used heavy gold to buy Su Wan, the daughter of a disgraced official, and took her as his strategist.
Su Wan understood his strategies and his ambitions; she was the resonance of his soul.
As for Shen Li, she only knew how to stand before him with a blade in hand, calling him a "good-for-nothing" while blocking fatal stray arrows for him.
Watching Shen Li covered in blood, a flicker of imperceptible pain flashed in Xiao Cheng's eyes, yet he turned and took Su Wan's hand instead.
He had clearly seen the burning heat beneath Shen Li's icy exterior, yet he chose to play deaf and dumb.
Because the path of an emperor cannot have a soft spot; and Shen Li, as it happened, was his most fatal weakness.
"I plotted for the world for your sake, yet you promised her a lifetime of splendor."
"Shen Li, I never said I loved you. It was you who chose to believe it."

chapters.title: A Wedding Night?
chapters.content:
The night was deep, and the dew was heavy.

The wedding chamber was quiet, save for the flickering flames of the dragon-and-phoenix candles, casting red light across the walls.

The last of the well-wishing palace servants bowed and retreated. The heavy palace doors closed with a creak, shutting out the noise from outside.

On the wedding bed sat a woman adorned in a phoenix coronet and ceremonial robes.

She wore no veil. Her face was coldly beautiful, devoid of makeup. Her phoenix eyes were long and narrow; when she fixed her gaze on someone, it carried a genuine intensity, like a blade drawn from its sheath. The cumbersome and ornate wedding dress did not add a hint of feminine softness to her; instead, set off by the murderous aura she carried from crawling out of piles of corpses, it looked like a suit of cold armor.

She was the Great Zhou’s female war god, the only daughter of the Duke of Zhen, Shen Li.

In the corner of the room, a man dressed in bright red wedding robes stood at a loss, his head bowed so low he seemed to want to shrink into the cracks of the floor.

He was the current Emperor’s seventh son, Prince Cheng, Xiao Cheng.

A good-for-nothing recognized by the entire capital, a coward whom even the servants would spit upon behind his back.

The room fell silent, even their breathing grew light.

Shen Li slowly raised her eyes, her cold gaze landing on the man who dared not even lift his head.

This was her future husband.

A single imperial decree, a ridiculous arranged marriage, had wed her—a military tiger who guarded the northern borders and held great power—to this notoriously timid and weak prince.

The entire capital was watching the joke.

Watching how the Shen family, having achieved too much, ended up with a marriage to a good-for-nothing.

Watching how Shen Li, this tiger of the northern borders, would be locked inside this golden cage.

The humiliation felt like red-hot iron needles piercing Shen Li’s heart, one by one.

She stood up slowly. The pearls and jade on her phoenix coronet jingled with her movements, sounding jarringly sharp in the deathly silent room.

Xiao Cheng’s body trembled imperceptibly, and he bowed his head even lower.

Shen Li walked toward him step by step. Her high-heeled wedding shoes clicked against the smooth gold bricks—*da, da, da*—each sound like a step on Xiao Cheng’s heart.

She stopped in front of him.

"Look up." Her voice was flat, yet carried a force that brooked no refusal.

Xiao Cheng stiffened, his body shaking more violently, but he still dared not look up.

"I said, look up." Shen Li’s voice grew colder.

Only then did Xiao Cheng, as if frightened out of his wits, suddenly lift his head.

It was a face of peerless handsomeness, with delicate features and a high nose bridge. But at this moment, his face was filled with terror and servility, his beautiful eyes brimming with moisture, as if he were about to cry at any second.

He looked at Shen Li, his lips trembling, unable to utter a single word.

"Hah." Shen Li let out a cold, mocking laugh.

She suddenly raised her hand.

A flash of silver light flew from her sleeve like lightning!

*Whoosh!*

A sharp sound of air being pierced rang out!

Xiao Cheng was struck with terror. He stood frozen to the spot, not even knowing how to dodge, and could only watch helplessly as the cold light flew straight toward his face!

*Clang!*

A crisp, dull thud of a dagger embedding itself into wood!

A sharp dagger had grazed his ear and buried itself deep into the purple sandalwood pillar an inch behind him. The hilt was still vibrating, a testament to the force behind the throw.

A lock of severed hair drifted down from Xiao Cheng’s temple.

He felt a chill rise from his back.

His legs went weak, and with a *thump*, he actually fell straight to his knees.

"P-Princess... spare me... please spare me..."

He was deathly pale, unable to speak clearly, and kept kowtowing, his voice thick with sobs.

Shen Li looked down at him from above, her eyes devoid of pity, filled only with growing contempt.

"Xiao Cheng," she said slowly, enunciating his name syllable by syllable, "tell me, by what right do you marry me?"

"By the fact that you are a coward who can't even speak clearly? Or by the fact that you are a good-for-nothing who only knows how to cry in front of others?"

"Do you know that because of you, I, Shen Li, have become the biggest joke in the world! The glory that my Shen family of generals earned with blood over three generations has become the laughingstock of the capital!"

Every word was like a cold blade, mercilessly stabbing at Xiao Cheng’s self-esteem.

"I... I am not... I didn't..." Xiao Cheng shook his head frantically, tears actually streaming down his face. He babbled incoherently in his defense, "It... it was the Emperor's decree... I... I dared not disobey... Princess, I really didn't mean to..."

"I swear! From now on... I will never dare to offend you in the slightest! Whatever you tell me to do, I will do..."

As he cried, he crawled forward on his knees, trying to grab the hem of Shen Li’s skirt, only to be kicked away by her in disgust.

"Don't touch me!"

Shen Li’s voice was as cold as the wind and snow of the northern borders.

Xiao Cheng stumbled and fell to the ground. He didn't dare cry out in pain; he just lay there, shivering into a ball, emitting muffled whimpers like a small animal.

Watching him in this pathetic, hopeless state, the last shred of curiosity in Shen Li’s heart vanished.

She had thought that even if the Emperor were foolish, he wouldn't have saddled her with an absolute good-for-nothing. She had suspected there was some hidden truth she didn't know.

Now it seemed she had overthought it.

A good-for-nothing is just a good-for-nothing.

He was beyond saving.

"From today on, you sleep on the floor." Shen Li dropped the cold command, stopped looking at him, and turned toward the wedding bed.

"Yes... yes..." As if granted an amnesty, Xiao Cheng scrambled up from the floor, using his hands and feet to fetch a thin quilt from the corner to make a pallet on the floor.

He was as servile as a dog wagging its tail.

Shen Li pulled off the heavy phoenix coronet and tossed it onto the table with a loud *clatter*. With her back to Xiao Cheng, she began to undo her cumbersome wedding dress.

Just then.

"Ah!"

A short, sharp cry came from behind her.

Followed by the loud *crash* of porcelain shattering.

Shen Li turned around abruptly, only to see that Xiao Cheng, somehow, had "accidentally" bumped into the table, sweeping the jade pot filled with nuptial wine onto the floor.

The jade pot shattered into pieces.

Blood-red wine splashed everywhere, spreading across the floor in a sticky, dark red pool.

Xiao Cheng looked as if he had been frightened out of his wits, staring blankly at the shards and the wine, his face turning pale in an instant.

"I... I didn't mean to... Princess... I really didn't mean to..."

He scrambled to crouch down, trying to pick up the sharp shards with his hands.

Shen Li’s brow furrowed even deeper.

Useless.

Her disgust reached its peak.

She did not notice.

The moment he crouched down with his back to her, the terror and panic in Xiao Cheng’s eyes vanished completely.

Replacing it was a cold, sharp, and unfathomable depth.

His fingers, which appeared to be aimlessly scratching through the sticky wine, were actually using an extremely fast, complex technique invisible to outsiders to quickly trace a few subtle, broken lines in the blood-red liquid.

It was an order.

An order to the private army he had kept hidden for ten years.

Once done, the expression on his face instantly reverted to that of a panicked, useless fool.

He looked up at Shen Li, his face covered in tear tracks, his voice trembling: "Princess... I'm sorry... I... I spilled the nuptial wine... am I... am I going to be beheaded..."

Shen Li looked at the mess on the floor, then at his face, which was written all over with "stupid" and "useless," and the last of her anger turned into deep exhaustion.

Bickering with such an idiot would only lower her own status.

"Good-for-nothing."

She spat out the two words coldly. Ignoring the mess on the floor and the shivering man, she walked to the bed, took off her outer robe, and lay down fully clothed.

She closed her eyes, forcing herself to stop thinking about this humiliating situation.

The wedding chamber fell quiet again.

Only the sound of Xiao Cheng’s suppressed, intermittent sobbing remained.

And on the highest ridge of the Prince's mansion, a black shadow crouched behind the tiles like a ghost.

His gaze, through a gap in the window, precisely caught the strange, wine-drawn pattern on the floor.

The shadow’s body shuddered.

The next second, he stood up silently, knelt on one knee in the direction of the bridal chamber, and respectfully kowtowed.

Then, like a feather melting into the night, he vanished without a sound into the vast darkness.

The long night had only just begun.

chapters.title: So Much for Royal Dignity? How Did You Become the Laughingstock of the Capital!
chapters.content:
Shen Li opened her eyes abruptly. The instinct honed by years of licking blood from the edge of a blade caused the muscles in her right hand to tense instantly, almost gripping the dagger hidden beneath her pillow.

Killing intent.

Although extremely faint and fleeting, she had still sensed it.

She followed the sensation and looked over. The man who should have been curled up in a corner, sobbing in a low voice, had stood up at some point and was now standing with his back to her.

The flickering light of the festive dragon-and-phoenix candles cast his silhouette onto the wall. He was still wearing that oversized wedding robe, head bowed, his expression unreadable.

There was no crying, nor was there any trembling.

He stood there quietly, like a sculpture merged into the darkness. The faint trace of killing intent from a moment ago seemed like nothing more than an illusion left over from Shen Li’s many years on the battlefield.

The air was deathly still; even the sound of the wind outside the window had ceased.

Shen Li’s brows furrowed tightly.

This man was not right.

Just as she was about to speak to test him, the "sculpture" moved.

He seemed stung by her gaze; his body gave an imperceptible shudder, and the silence was instantly broken. He turned around abruptly, his movements flustered, like a deer in the forest startled by a noise.

"Pri... Princess Consort... Did I... did I disturb you?"

His voice was thick with nasal congestion and the remnants of unspent tears, cautious and filled with humble fear. He raised his head, and his face was indeed covered in tear tracks, his eyes red and swollen. Paired with his naturally handsome features, he appeared even more annoyingly fragile.

"I... I will leave at once, I certainly won't be an eyesore to you..."

As he spoke, he actually scrambled toward the door on his hands and knees, almost fleeing. He pulled the door open, allowing the cold night air to rush in, and his figure quickly disappeared outside.

Shen Li’s clenched fist slowly relaxed.

Watching his panicked retreating back, the sharpness in her eyes finally turned into a trace of suspicion and even deeper contempt.

An illusion?

For that split second just now, she had almost thought she was facing a dormant beast that had retracted all its claws and fangs. But looking at him now, he was still that hopeless piece of trash.

She could even hear his suppressed coughing outside the door and the faint, intermittent sobbing in the cold wind.

"Useless thing."

Shen Li gave a cold snort, turned over, and forced herself to close her eyes.

This night was destined to be spent in light sleep.

The next day, before dawn had broken, Nanny Zhang, sent by the palace to instruct them on etiquette, was already urging them loudly outside the door, her words filled with undisguised disdain. On the first day of marriage, one must enter the palace to offer tea to the Emperor and Empress; this was the rule.

Shen Li pushed the door open and immediately saw Xiao Cheng standing in the shadow of a corridor pillar, wearing two massive dark circles under his eyes. He was cowering, covered in the morning dew, clearly having stood outside all night.

Seeing Shen Li, he shrank behind the pillar instinctively, like a mouse seeing a cat.

Shen Li couldn't be bothered to waste a glance on him and walked straight toward the prepared princely carriage.

The journey was silent; the atmosphere inside the carriage was colder than a Siberian wind.

Upon arriving at the palace gate, the two switched to a palanquin, one after the other, heading for the Empress’s Fengyi Palace.

Inside Fengyi Palace, the place was already bustling with noise.

Emperor Xiao Yuan sat upright in the main seat, his dragon robe majestic, while the Empress beside him whispered to him with a smile. The Crown Prince, Xiao Rui, the Third Prince, Xiao Xian, and several other adult princes were all present, chatting and laughing with familiar nobles of the imperial clan. Their gazes drifted toward the hall entrance from time to time, their expressions of anticipation for a good show undisguised.

When the eunuch drew out his voice to announce, "The Seventh Prince and the Seventh Princess Consort have arrived—," the entire hall fell silent instantly.

Dozens of gazes, like searchlights, were cast upon them in unison, mixed with curiosity and sympathy, but mostly, naked schadenfreude.

Xiao Cheng kept his head bowed, following half a step behind Shen Li, walking in lockstep. His unpresentable, "little wife" demeanor instantly drew a burst of undisguised sneers from several of the princes.

"Yo, Seventh Brother is here." It was the Crown Prince, Xiao Rui, who spoke. His face was as handsome as jade, and he smiled playfully, yet his eyes looked down on them with the contempt one might reserve for ants. "The wedding night was surely short and sweet; you must be exhausted, right?"

Xiao Cheng buried his head even lower, his lips trembling, unable to utter a single word.

"Big Brother is joking."

Shen Li stepped forward expressionlessly, ignoring the Crown Prince, and gave a slight nod to the Emperor and Empress above, her voice as cold as ice: "Shen Li pays her respects to Your Majesty and the Empress."

She did not perform the full kowtow; a simple nod was the privilege of the General who Defends the Nation. This seemingly disrespectful act caused the smile on the Crown Prince's face to stiffen; he was choked with displeasure.

"Look at Seventh Brother’s absent-minded appearance," the Third Prince, Xiao Xian, chimed in with a strange laugh, fanning the flames. "Could it be that our Great Zhou’s famous 'Female War God' treated the bedroom like a battlefield, and you, Seventh Brother, suffered a defeat and were kicked out of the room?"

"Hahahaha!"

As soon as these words were spoken, the hall erupted in laughter. Even the Emperor on the dragon throne had a faint, imperceptible curve at the corner of his mouth.

In their eyes, this absurd marriage was merely a play staged by the royal family to appease military power, and Xiao Cheng, this piece of trash, was the biggest joke in the play.

Xiao Cheng’s face turned the color of a pig’s liver. His hands gripped his sleeves tightly, his body trembling slightly from humiliation, yet he dared not even raise his head.

Shen Li’s expression also sank completely, cold light flashing in her phoenix eyes.

Just then, the Master of Ceremonies shouted: "The auspicious hour has arrived, the newlyweds shall offer tea—"

A maidservant stepped forward with a tea tray. According to the rules, Xiao Cheng was to offer tea first. He tremblingly picked up a cup of tea, preparing to present it to the Emperor.

He had to pass by the seats of the Crown Prince and the Third Prince.

"Wait."

Crown Prince Xiao Rui suddenly spoke. He stood up unhurriedly, his gaze sweeping over Xiao Cheng with the playfulness of a cat playing with a mouse.

"Seventh Brother, Father is the Supreme Ruler. For you to look so wretched and listless is a great disrespect to Father. This first cup of tea should be offered to this Prince, so that I may test the temperature for you and see if your heart is sincere, lest you offend Father."

As soon as these words were out, everyone was stunned for a moment, then revealed knowing, wicked smiles.

This was an unheard-of rule! Since when does a Crown Prince make his younger brother offer him tea first? This was clearly a public humiliation!

The Master of Ceremonies turned pale, wanting to say something, but after meeting the Crown Prince’s cold, chilling gaze, he obediently shut his mouth.

Xiao Cheng froze in place, his hand holding the teacup shaking even more violently, spilling a few drops of hot tea onto the back of his hand.

"What? Is Seventh Brother unwilling?" The smile on the Crown Prince’s face grew wider. "Or is it that in your heart, this Prince, the Crown Prince, is not worthy of drinking this cup of tea from you?"

A heavy accusation was placed directly upon him!

Xiao Cheng was scared out of his wits, his face deathly pale. He shook his head frantically, stuttering, "No... that’s not it, Big Brother, I..."

"Then hurry up." The Crown Prince urged impatiently.

Humiliating tears welled up in Xiao Cheng’s eyes. He knew that he would lose face today for sure. Gritting his teeth, he held the tea and shuffled step by step toward the Crown Prince, preparing to kneel.

Just as his knees were about to touch the floor—

"Slap!"

A crisp sound of a slap echoed throughout the deathly silent hall!

Everyone watched in horror as Shen Li, who had reached the Crown Prince at some point, landed a solid slap across his face!

Fast! It was too fast! So fast that no one could react!

The Crown Prince’s handsome face swelled up at a speed visible to the naked eye, and a clear five-fingered print appeared on it. He was completely stunned, clutching his face and looking at Shen Li in disbelief.

"You... how dare you hit me?!"

Shen Li withdrew her hand, not even bothering to look at him. Her cold gaze swept across the hall and finally settled on the Emperor, who was also looking on in shock from the dragon throne.

"Your Majesty," she said slowly, her voice not loud, but every word like a blade, carrying the iron-blooded aura of a thousand armies, "According to our dynasty’s rites, when a new bride offers tea, there is an order of seniority, and heaven and earth are the foundation. The Crown Prince openly defies the rules of our ancestors, forcing his younger brother to perform an improper rite; this is unbrotherly! Furthermore, in your presence, he disrupts the order of the court; this is disloyal!"

She paused, then turned sharply toward the Crown Prince, her phoenix eyes like lightning!

"I am disciplining you on behalf of His Majesty; do you have any objections?"

The entire Fengyi Palace was deathly silent! You could hear a pin drop!

Everyone was stunned by Shen Li’s thunderous methods and heart-piercing words. No one expected that she would dare to strike directly and even bring out such heavy labels as "disloyal and unfilial"!

The Crown Prince’s face turned from blue to white. He wanted to lash out, but the words "disloyal and unbrotherly" weighed on his head like four mountains, leaving him unable to refute a single word! In front of his father, what could he say? That he just wanted to humiliate his younger brother?

Shen Li didn't even look at him. She turned, took the tea from the stunned Xiao Cheng, picked up another cup, and walked straight to the Emperor and Empress, her posture composed, as if nothing had just happened.

"Your Majesty, Empress, please have some tea."

Emperor Xiao Yuan looked deeply at the defiant daughter-in-law before him, his eyes dark and unreadable. After a long while, he spoke slowly, his voice devoid of joy or anger:

"Good... a very good daughter of the General who Defends the Nation."

He finally took the tea.

This farce ended in such a shocking way.

Xiao Cheng crawled up from the ground, still shaken, and hid behind Shen Li. In a voice only the two of them could hear, he said tremblingly, "Th... thank you, Princess Consort..."

The cowardice and dependency in that tone made Shen Li feel a physiological sense of disgust.

She did not turn back, replying in an equally low, bone-chilling voice:

"I am not protecting you; I am protecting the face of the General who Defends the Nation."

"Shut your mouth, don't make me feel sick."

chapters.title: The Prince’s "Calculation"
chapters.content:
In the two days since returning from offering tea at the palace, the entire Prince Cheng’s Mansion had been plunged into a strange, low-pressure atmosphere.

The servants walked on tiptoe, not daring to make the slightest sound, and even their breathing was cautious.

For no other reason than that their Princess Consort, that legendary "Female War God," had given the Crown Prince a solid slap in the face in Fengyi Palace, right in front of the Emperor and the entire imperial clan.

This news spread through every street and alley of the capital within a single day.

The storytellers in the teahouses embellished their tales, painting Shen Li as a fiery woman who stood up for her husband and defied the powerful. Meanwhile, the self-proclaimed refined aristocratic clans mocked the Crown Prince in private for his incompetence in being publicly humiliated by a woman, and they scorned the Seventh Prince, Xiao Cheng, as a spineless coward who could only hide behind his wife’s skirts.

For a time, the Prince Cheng Residence became the center of the capital’s biggest jokes.

Shen Li remained indifferent to all of this.

She continued to practice her saber techniques in the training grounds, every move and stance carrying a sharp, biting wind. Only in this way could she slightly alleviate the restlessness in her heart.

She was not protecting Xiao Cheng.

She was protecting the century-old reputation of the General of the State’s residence, the honor earned by three generations of the Shen family with their blood.

Her husband could be a good-for-nothing, but he must never be trampled underfoot by others in public. Because to slap his face was to slap hers, and to slap the face of the entire Shen family.

Whenever she thought of the man hiding behind her, looking so pathetically grateful and cowardly, she felt waves of nausea.

"Pr... Princess Consort..."

A timid voice interrupted her thoughts.

Shen Li sheathed her saber and stood still, the light sweat on her forehead glistening in the sun. She didn't need to turn around to know who it was.

Aside from Xiao Cheng, no one in this residence dared to speak to her in such a terrified tone.

She didn't respond, merely using a cloth to slowly wipe the blade of the precious saber in her hand. The blade was as smooth as a mirror, reflecting her cold, detached profile.

Seeing her ignore him, Xiao Cheng gathered his courage to take two more steps forward, his voice even softer.

"The day before yesterday... thank you for coming to my rescue, Princess Consort. I... I have no way to repay you..."

He spoke stumblingly, like a child who had forgotten his lines.

"I... I want to... do something for you."

Shen Li’s wiping motion paused, and she finally turned around, looking at him coldly.

"What could you possibly do for me?" Her tone was filled with disdain. "Can you go to the battlefield to kill enemies for me, or can you protect the safety of my General’s residence?"

Xiao Cheng shuddered under her gaze and lowered his head again.

"I... I cannot..." his voice was very small, "but... yesterday I heard the servants say that when you were dressing, you lacked a suitable jade hairpin..."

Shen Li frowned.

She had indeed complained casually yesterday that the hairpins made by the capital’s jewelers were either too gaudy or too fragile, far less practical than the bone hairpins used in the military.

"I... I know that 'Zhenbao Zhai' in the east of the city has just received a batch of top-quality Hetian jade. I want... I want to go pick one out for you... as... as my token of gratitude..."

After he finished speaking, he looked up, his eyes filled with hope and fawning, like a pet begging for its master's favor.

That look made Shen Li feel a wave of disgust.

For some reason, the refusal that had reached her lips was swallowed back down.

Perhaps it was because she had been too stifled in the residence these past few days, or perhaps she wanted to see what else this "useless" man could do besides crying and kneeling.

"Prepare the carriage."

She dropped these two words coldly and turned to return to her room to change.

Behind her, Xiao Cheng looked as if he had been granted a pardon, his face showing a near-stupid joy.

Half an hour later, the Prince Cheng Residence’s carriage, escorted by a team of Shen family guards, slowly drove toward the capital’s most bustling Zhuque Street.

Zhenbao Zhai was the most famous jewelry store in the capital, frequented only by the rich and noble.

The shopkeeper was a slick and experienced man. Upon seeing the Seventh Prince and his Princess Consort arrive, he hurried out to greet them personally, his face wreathed in smiles.

"I didn't know the Prince and Princess Consort were coming! Please forgive me for failing to welcome you properly!"

Xiao Cheng was clearly uncomfortable with such scenes; he just nodded stiffly and hid to the side.

Shen Li, however, was long accustomed to this. She walked straight to the counter displaying the jade and scanned them one by one.

The jade hairpins here were indeed exquisite, with masterful carving. However, she felt that most were carved with overly complex phoenixes or peonies, or adorned with jingling tassels—gorgeous, yes, but lacking in character.

She watched with little interest.

"Princess Consort, how about this one?"

Xiao Cheng had approached at some point, holding a brocade box, carefully presenting it to her.

Shen Li lowered her eyes to look.

Inside the box lay a jade hairpin.

The hairpin was carved from a single piece of flawless mutton-fat jade. It had no unnecessary ornamentation, save for a single, sketch-like carving of a plum blossom bud at the tip.

Simple, elegant, yet possessing a cold and aloof spirit.

For the first time, a subtle ripple appeared in Shen Li’s eyes.

This hairpin was indeed to her liking.

She didn't look at Xiao Cheng, but said coolly to the shopkeeper, "I'll take this one."

"Very well!" The shopkeeper beamed. "The Princess Consort has a wonderful eye! This is the final masterpiece of our shop’s master jade carver, named 'Treading Snow.' It is the perfect match for a person of such peerless elegance as yourself!"

Just as Xiao Cheng was about to pay, an arrogant voice came from the entrance.

"Hold it! I want this hairpin!"

Everyone turned to look. A young man in a sapphire brocade robe, waving a flamboyant folding fan and surrounded by a group of servants, swaggered in.

The shopkeeper’s expression changed slightly when he saw the newcomer, but he still stepped forward with a forced smile.

"Ah, Young Master Qian, what wind has blown you here?"

The man was Qian Feng, the only son of the Minister of Personnel, Qian Qian. Relying on his father’s power, he was notorious in the capital for his bullying.

Qian Feng ignored the shopkeeper entirely. His small eyes leered at Shen Li before landing on the jade hairpin, his eyes filled with greed.

"I said, I want this hairpin." He pointed his fan at the brocade box, his tone brook no argument. "Name your price."

The shopkeeper wiped away cold sweat and said awkwardly, "Young Master Qian, it is truly unfortunate, but this hairpin has already been... purchased by the Seventh Prince and the Princess Consort."

"The Seventh Prince?" Qian Feng only then noticed Xiao Cheng. He looked Xiao Cheng up and down, his expression shifting from confusion to realization, and finally, to undisguised contempt.

"Oh—so it’s that useless prince who lives off his wife!"

He deliberately drew out his voice, drawing a burst of mocking laughter from his servants.

"Tell me, shopkeeper, are you mistaken?" Qian Feng tapped the shopkeeper’s face with his fan. "He’s a loser who even has to hand his salary over to his wife; where would he get the money for such an expensive hairpin? Don't tell me he’s trying to dine and dash here?"

The insult was incredibly crude.

Xiao Cheng’s face turned bright red instantly, his fists clenched tightly, his body trembling slightly from anger and fear.

Shen Li’s expression turned icy in an instant.

The two Shen family guards behind her had already gripped their saber hilts, staring at Qian Feng with hostile intent.

"Insolent!" one guard shouted sharply, "How dare you be disrespectful to the Prince!"

Qian Feng, however, was fearless. The dozen servants behind him swarmed forward with a clatter, each brandishing clubs, confronting the two guards with an absolute advantage in numbers.

"What? Want to fight?" Qian Feng sneered. "I’ll say it right here: I’ve taken a liking to this hairpin. If you’re smart, you’ll hand it over and kowtow to apologize, otherwise, none of you are leaving this door today!"

The atmosphere turned tense in an instant.

The onlookers had long since fled in fear.

Murderous intent surfaced in Shen Li’s eyes.

A mere son of a Minister dared to be this arrogant.

She took a step forward, and the aura she emitted caused the air in Zhenbao Zhai to stagnate.

"It seems I have stayed in the capital for too long, and some people have forgotten what this blade of mine is for."

Her voice was soft, but it carried the scent of blood.

Qian Feng was intimidated by her presence and subconsciously took a step back, but then he stiffened his neck and shouted, "You... you dare! In broad daylight, you would dare to commit murder? My father is the Minister of Personnel!"

"Minister?" Shen Li laughed, a smile colder than tears. "The barbarian commanders I’ve killed held higher ranks than your father."

Before the words had even faded, she prepared to strike.

At this critical moment:

"Don't... don't fight!"

A cry with a sob came from behind Shen Li.

Xiao Cheng looked terrified, frantically digging into his robes.

"I have money... I have money... please don't fight..."

He seemed to be trying to pull out a coin purse, but his movements were incredibly clumsy due to his panic.

*Clatter!*

A crisp sound rang out.

A heavy, golden object slid from his wide sleeve and fell onto the smooth bluestone floor, emitting a clear, loud impact.

It was a token made of pure gold.

The token bounced twice on the floor, finally landing face-up, resting steadily at Qian Feng’s feet.

The afternoon sun shone through the windows, landing right on the gold token.

On the token, dragon patterns coiled around four characters that shimmered in the sunlight.

*AS IF THE EMPEROR WERE PRESENT!*

Time seemed to freeze.

The shop went deathly silent.

Qian Feng, who had been incredibly arrogant a second ago, turned deathly pale the moment he saw those four characters.

His facial muscles twitched uncontrollably, his small eyes widened, his mouth hung open, and a "gurgling" sound came from his throat, but he couldn't utter a single word.

*Thump!*

The next second, his legs gave way, and he knelt down straight.

The servants behind him were already scared out of their wits; they dropped their clubs and scrambled to kneel on the ground, shivering.

"Pr... Prince, spare me! Prince, spare me!"

Once Qian Feng realized what was happening, he began kowtowing frantically while slapping his own face, crying out, "This lowly one had eyes but failed to recognize greatness! This lowly one deserves to die! I will never dare again!"

The sound of his head hitting the floor was rhythmic and loud; within a few moments, his forehead was already bleeding.

The entire scene had undergone a complete reversal.

Shen Li’s hand, poised to strike, froze in mid-air.

She looked at the glaring gold token on the floor, then at the pathetic, groveling Qian Feng, and finally, her gaze fell upon Xiao Cheng, who still wore a look of "utter panic."

Her mood was complicated.

There was a sense of vindication, but more than that, an indescribable disdain.

A bloodless victory.

Without even having to utter a single harsh word.

Relying solely on a token, he had forced an opponent who was just moments ago insufferably arrogant to kneel on the ground and beg for mercy like a cur.

This was indeed a victory.

In her eyes, however, such a victory was cowardly and shameful.

Borrowing the tiger's might to intimidate.

Borrowed power, in the end, is never one's own.

This man, from beginning to end, was only capable of such underhanded, dishonorable tactics.

She, Shen Li, disdained to act in such a way.

"Your... Your Highness..." Xiao Cheng pretended to be terrified by the scene before him. He picked up the gold token, shoved it back into his robes in a panic, and then ran to Shen Li’s side, clutching her sleeve, his voice trembling. "We... we should leave quickly... I’m scared..."

Shen Li shook his hand off in disgust.

Without even glancing at Qian Feng, who was kneeling on the ground, she took the jade hairpin the shopkeeper had already packed and turned to leave.

Xiao Cheng hurried to follow.

Behind them lay the sound of Qian Feng’s heart-wrenching pleas and the deathly silence of the Treasure Pavilion.

In the carriage on the way back, Xiao Cheng continued to pat his chest as if still shaken, maintaining the appearance of someone who had not yet recovered from the fright.

Shen Li sat with her arms crossed, eyes closed, resting in silence.

She did not see.

She did not see that the moment Xiao Cheng lowered his eyes, a flash of coldness flickered deep within his supposedly terrified gaze.

She protects me once.

Then I shall let every jackal and wolf in this capital know that she, Shen Li, is my wife. To touch me is to touch the General of the State’s mansion.

The Emperor’s decree of marriage was intended to use the fierce tiger that is the Shen family to keep watch over the sheep that is me.

Now, I will make this tiger, whether willingly or unwillingly, become my most impenetrable shield.

What she protects is the face of the Shen family.

And what I want is for the entire Shen family to be drawn into my game.

chapters.title: Yanyu Pavilion
chapters.content:
The farce at the Treasure Pavilion was like a stone cast into the deep waters of the capital, the ripples refusing to settle for a long time.

The appearance of the "As If I Were Present" gold token caused the Minister of Personnel, Qian Qian, to break his own useless son’s legs that very night. The next day, he had his son carried to the Prince Cheng mansion to beg for forgiveness, offering up nearly half of the Qian family’s fortune as compensation.

Xiao Cheng, "too terrified" to show his face, left the entire reception to a cold-faced Shen Li.

This series of events caused the political climate of the capital to take a bizarre turn.

On the surface, no one dared to criticize the Seventh Prince to his face. After all, if even the Crown Prince had to avoid the edge of the "As If I Were Present" token, who would dare court such disaster?

Yet, in the shadows, even more sordid rumors grew like weeds in a gutter.

"Have you heard? The Seventh Prince is quite the big shot now, even daring to defy the Crown Prince!"

"Big shot? Big shot my foot! Isn't it all because of the Princess Consort and her father, the Duke of the State? When it comes down to it, he’s just a man living off his wife!"

"Exactly! I heard he takes the money he squeezes out of the Princess Consort and spends his days at Yanyu Pavilion, enjoying himself so much he’s forgotten his home!"

"Is that true? Yanyu Pavilion is the biggest money-sink in the capital! Isn't he afraid the Princess Consort will break his legs?"

"Afraid? He’s got the gold token to protect him now; his wings have hardened! Besides, that eldest daughter of the Shen family is like a tomboy—what man could stand her? If it were me, I’d go to Yanyu Pavilion to find a soft bed too, ha ha ha..."

The filthy, unbearable gossip spread on the wind to every corner of the capital, and naturally, it eventually reached the ears of the General of the State’s mansion and the Prince Cheng mansion.

On the training grounds.

"Crack!"

Shen Li swung her blade, the sharp edge whistling through the air, cleanly slicing a wooden training dummy—thick enough for a man to wrap his arms around—into two pieces!

Uncle Zhang, the captain of the personal guards standing nearby, felt his eyelids twitch.

He had been by Shen Li’s side for ten years, having crawled out of piles of corpses in the Northern Frontier with her; he understood his young mistress’s temper better than anyone.

The angrier she was, the calmer she appeared on the surface; only the blade in her hand would reveal the monstrous killing intent.

"Mistress," Uncle Zhang said, steeling himself as he stepped forward to hand over a piece of intelligence. "The matter you asked us to investigate... we have leads."

"The Seventh Prince... is indeed a regular at Yanyu Pavilion. Every time he goes, he reserves the most expensive 'Heavenly Room Number One,' and he stays for the entire afternoon."

Shen Li took the report without looking at it and crushed it in her palm; the thin paper turned to dust.

"Good."

Her voice betrayed no emotion.

"A fine Xiao Cheng."

She protected him, but not so he could use her favor as a pretext to go out and tarnish the reputation of her Shen family!

She had thought that the previous two warnings would at least make him behave.

She had not expected that instead of restraining himself, he would only become more brazen!

Languishing in brothels, staying out all night.

Whose face was he slapping?

He was dragging her name, Shen Li, and the reputation of the entire General of the State’s mansion through the mud, letting everyone in the capital trample upon it at will!

"Prepare the horses!"

Shen Li sheathed her sword, her voice as cold as the snows of the Northern Frontier.

"I want to see if the 'soft bed' of Yanyu Pavilion is tougher than the blade in my hand!"

That night, as the lanterns were lit.

As the most renowned den of indulgence in the capital, Yanyu Pavilion was entering its liveliest hour of the day.

The building was intricately carved and brightly lit. Inside, the music of strings and flutes played, the scent of wine wafted through the air, and dancers in revealing attire swayed their serpentine waists. Wealthy merchants and young nobles threw money away like dirt, lost in drunken dreams.

Amidst this atmosphere of luxury, a group of uninvited guests, like a drawn sword, pierced through the facade of prosperity.

Shen Li wore black martial attire, her long hair tied up high, her unadorned face covered in a layer of frost.

She did not bring a large force; only Uncle Zhang and four other personal guards followed her. But these five were battle-hardened elites who had survived mountains of corpses and seas of blood; the aura they exuded was more effective than a hundred household servants.

The moment they appeared, the lewd smiles on the faces of the pimps at the entrance of Yanyu Pavilion froze instantly.

"A... a few guests, are you here to listen to music or..."

"Get lost."

Shen Li said only two words.

The pimp felt a wave of killing intent rush toward him, making him feel as if he had fallen into an ice cellar. His legs went weak, and he collapsed to the ground uncontrollably.

Shen Li did not even look at him, stepping directly into the doors of Yanyu Pavilion.

Her party stood in stark contrast to the debauched atmosphere of the building.

The noisy music and laughter in the main hall fell into a momentary silence due to their intrusion.

Everyone’s gaze was drawn to this woman radiating such fierce, murderous intent.

A middle-aged procuress, still possessing a certain charm, hurried over, waving her scented handkerchief vigorously.

"Oh my, this guest, you look quite unfamiliar. Is this your first time at our Yanyu Pavilion? Our girls, whether slender or curvaceous, have it all; we guarantee you'll be satisfied..."

"Where is Xiao Cheng?"

Shen Li cut through her nonsense directly.

The smile on the procuress's face stiffened. Her eyes darted around, and she immediately put on a look of distress.

"Sir, you must be joking. We have so many guests coming and going, how could I remember who is who... Besides, as servants, we wouldn't dare pry into the identities of our guests, would we?"

She spoke with a forced laugh, but her heart was churning with a storm.

Xiao Cheng! The Seventh Prince!

Could this woman be...

"Heavenly Room Number One."

Shen Li had no patience for her chatter and stated the room number directly.

The procuress’s expression changed completely.

"Sir... the guest in Heavenly Room Number One... is of noble status. Without... without his orders, no one is allowed to disturb him..."

"Is that so?"

Shen Li sneered.

In the next second, her figure flickered.

Before anyone could react, she was already behind the procuress.

A dagger was pressed silently against the procuress's back.

"I will say it again: take me there."

"Otherwise, your heart will be colder than this blade."

The icy touch and the emotionless words made the procuress's blood feel as though it had frozen. She could feel the dagger piercing through her expensive silk outer garment; one more inch, and it would take her life.

"It's... it's on the third floor... the... the very last room..."

The procuress's voice trembled like a sieve.

Shen Li withdrew the dagger and wiped it on the procuress's clothes, as if she had touched something filthy.

Ignoring the woman who had collapsed in terror, she walked straight toward the third floor.

Wherever she passed, the crowd parted.

The third floor was indeed much quieter than the floor below.

The air was filled with a more expensive incense.

The room at the very end had a door made of fine golden nanmu wood, with a gilded plaque hanging above it, inscribed with three bold, dragon-like characters.

Heavenly Room Number One.

Standing at the entrance were two burly men with bulging temples—clearly experts in internal martial arts.

"Stop! There is a distinguished guest inside; you are not to disturb him!"

One of them reached out to block her, his tone firm.

Shen Li did not even glance at him.

She simply raised her foot.

"Bang—!"

A deafening sound!

The heavy door, crafted from a solid piece of golden nanmu and worth a thousand pieces of gold, was kicked open by her, splitting right down the middle!

Wood chips flew everywhere!

The two guards, acting like gatekeepers, were sent flying by the sheer force, rolling onto the ground and unable to get up for a long time.

Shen Li stepped into the room, radiating coldness.

She had already made up her mind.

Today, in front of everyone, she would drag this reckless waste out of his "soft bed" and show him exactly why the flowers were so red!

However, when she saw the scene inside the room, she was struck as if by lightning, frozen in place.

The debauched scene of a "wine pool and meat forest" she had imagined did not exist.

There were no singing girls, no distracting music, not even a trace of a woman's perfume.

The massive room was decorated with extreme simplicity. In the air, suddenly stilled by the sound of the kicked-in door, only a deathly silence remained.

In the center of the room stood a massive sand table.

On the table, mountains, rivers, cities, and mountain passes were depicted in meticulous detail—it was, in fact, a military topographical map of the entire Northern territory of the Great Zhou!

Several men dressed in coarse linen, appearing to be ordinary merchants, were staring at the doorway in astonishment. The solemn expressions they had worn while gathered around the sand table had not yet fully faded, replaced instead by a tempered vigilance.

Their eyes were as sharp as eagles', and their bodies, subconsciously tensed, stood as straight as pines. The iron-blooded aura of soldiers, emanating from their very bones, was exposed in this moment!

And directly in front of the sand table, the man who should have been dead-drunk in the arms of a beauty—her husband, Xiao Cheng—stood frozen in place.

He was not wearing his cumbersome prince’s ceremonial robes, but only a simple ink-colored long gown.

Under the candlelight, his side profile was well-defined, and those eyes, which usually held only cowardice and lewdness, now retained a trace of deep, sharp edge!

One of his fingers remained suspended over a mountain pass on the sand table, as if he had been pointing something out just a moment before the loud crash occurred.

In Shen Li’s ears, a steady and powerful voice seemed to still be echoing:

"One hundred and thirty miles east of Cangbei City lies Black Wind Pass... We must drive a nail into this position."

"Advancing, it can serve as an outpost for harassment; retreating, it can serve as a beacon tower for early warning."

That air of commanding the world, that strategic vision that held the entire war situation in the palm of his hand...

It struck Shen Li like a bolt of lightning!

This... was this the good-for-nothing who couldn't even speak clearly?

This... was this the spineless coward who only knew how to kneel and beg for mercy?

Just as her heart was shaken and she stood stunned at the doorway, Xiao Cheng seemed to sense something and slowly turned his head.

The moment he saw Shen Li, the composure on his face vanished completely!

Those eyes, deep as the starry sky, switched within a second to the terror and panic of a rabbit!

"Pr... Princess Consort!"

He let out a startled cry, like a cat whose tail had been stepped on, and scrambled in a panic to cover the massive sand table with his sleeves.

"You... why are you here?!"

He stammered incoherently, forcing a smile onto his face that looked worse than crying.

"I... I wasn't doing anything! I was just... just discussing, discussing the price of rice for Cangbei with some rice merchant friends! Yes! The price of rice!"

This excuse was so clumsy it was an insult to one's intelligence.

But Shen Li could not say a single word.

Her mind was a complete blank.

Before her eyes was Xiao Cheng’s panicked face, plastered with "I am a loser."

Yet in her mind, the scene from just a moment ago kept replaying—the way he had stood there, pointing at the sand table and speaking with such eloquence.

Two completely different figures were violently overlapping and tearing at each other in her mind!

She felt a wave of intense dizziness!

Fake.

It must be fake.

How could he possibly...

However, before she could recover from this massive shock:

"Bang—!"

A blast even louder than the last!

The door, already teetering from being kicked, was now shattered into fragments by an even greater external force!

Amidst the flying wood splinters, a figure clad in heavy armor with a ferocious grin on his face charged in with a large group of men, fierce as wolves and tigers!

The intruder was the Crown Prince’s confidant, Commander of the Capital Garrison, Li Mang!

Li Mang’s gaze swept across the room quickly. When he saw the massive sand table and the few "rice merchants" with their strange expressions, a flash of doubt crossed his eyes, but he immediately locked his gaze onto Xiao Cheng, who was "panickedly" hiding behind Shen Li.

He let out a sinister laugh and held high the Crown Prince’s command arrow in his hand.

"By order of the Crown Prince!"

"The Seventh Prince, Xiao Cheng, as an imperial son, thinks not of progress but engages in lewdness and debauchery in such a filthy place, disgracing the royal dignity!"

"Men! Take him!"

chapters.title: Diverting the Disaster
chapters.content:
The Commander of the Capital Garrison, Li Mang, was the number one lackey of Crown Prince Xiao Rui, notorious for his ruthlessness and known for obeying only the Crown Prince’s orders.

He had personally led a large force to break in, holding the gleaming Crown Prince’s command arrow high; his intent was self-evident.

This was revenge.

It was the most direct and vicious retaliation for that slap at the Fengyi Palace!

Caught in the act!

There was no charge more effective at completely destroying the reputation of a prince and a female general than this!

The Capital Garrison soldiers behind Li Mang swarmed in, instantly surrounding the "Heavenly Number One" room so tightly not even water could pass through. Their steel blades were unsheathed, glinting coldly, casting an eerie chill over the candlelight in the room.

The few "rice merchants" gathered around the sand table felt a murderous intent flash in their eyes the moment they realized the intruders were the Capital Garrison, and their hands subconsciously reached for their waists. Their movements stopped abruptly after receiving an extremely subtle, fleeting glance from Xiao Cheng.

Their straight backs instantly slumped, the sharpness in their eyes replaced by panic, and in an instant, they turned back into those honest-looking, terrified businessmen.

And at the center of this storm, Xiao Cheng displayed the fear expected of a "good-for-nothing."

"Ah!"

He let out a short, shrill scream, his entire body seeming to lose its bones as he scrambled and crawled to hide behind Shen Li, clutching her hem tightly, his body trembling like a leaf in the wind.

"Pr... Princess Consort... save me... I'm scared..."

The voice was tearful and sounded utterly desperate.

Shen Li ignored him.

She did not even turn her head to look at him.

Her entire focus was still immersed in the massive shock from just moments ago. The Xiao Cheng who commanded the world with steady poise and the Xiao Cheng before her who only knew how to tremble and beg for help—the two figures kept clashing in her mind, leaving her feeling deeply confused.

Instincts born from the battlefield led her to make the most direct reaction the moment Li Mang gave his order.

She stepped sideways, blocking everyone.

She did not draw her sword, yet the murderous aura she had honed on the battlefield was sharper than any unsheathed blade.

"Li Mang," her voice was icy, "you have a lot of nerve."

When Li Mang saw Shen Li, a flash of wariness crossed his face, but then he grinned ferociously. He knew Shen Li could fight, but this was the capital, under the Emperor’s feet, not the Northern battlefield where she could do as she pleased.

"General Shen, this subordinate is merely following orders." Li Mang deliberately emphasized the word "General," his tone dripping with mockery. "His Highness the Crown Prince has decreed that the Seventh Prince is meeting with bandits in such a den of vice, engaging in illicit acts, and disgracing the royal dignity—a crime that cannot be forgiven! This subordinate is ordered to make the arrest!"

He shook the command arrow in his hand, looking utterly fearless.

"General Shen, no matter how high your martial arts are, do you dare to defy the Crown Prince’s order and rescue a prisoner in public? That is a crime of treason!"

A heavy label of "treason" was slapped onto her just like that.

Uncle Zhang, the captain of Shen Li’s personal guards, and the others drew their swords with a "shing," confronting the Capital Garrison, and the atmosphere instantly turned tense.

"Put them away!" Shen Li commanded coldly.

Although Uncle Zhang and the others were unwilling, they obeyed the order and sheathed their swords.

Shen Li knew very well that Li Mang was speaking the truth.

She could strike the Crown Prince because that was a family matter, which the Emperor could suppress as "the antics of the younger generation."

She could not attack the Capital Garrison, nor could she defy the command arrow that represented the Crown Prince’s authority.

Once she made a move, it would confirm that the General’s Mansion was harboring military strength and disregarding imperial power, which would truly lead to an irredeemable situation.

The Crown Prince’s move was both poisonous and ruthless.

He had calculated that she, Shen Li, would be held back by fear of the consequences.

Seeing Shen Li fall silent, the smile on Li Mang’s face became even more triumphant.

"General Shen, you are a smart person. Is it worth sacrificing your entire General’s Mansion for a piece of trash like this?" He stepped forward and whispered, "His Highness said that as long as you step aside now, he can pretend he saw nothing. As for this piece of trash..."

His gaze drifted past Shen Li and landed on the figure still trembling behind her.

"...His Highness will make him understand what it means to wish for death."

A cold light flashed in Shen Li’s eyes.

Let her step aside?

Let her watch helplessly as her husband was dragged away by these people without any dignity, suffering every humiliation?

She might not care about Xiao Cheng’s life or death.

But she could not disregard the reputation of the Shen family!

If she left today, tomorrow, the General’s Mansion would become the biggest laughingstock in the world!

Just as murderous intent rose in her heart and she prepared to disregard everything and strike Li Mang down, a sudden change occurred!

"Ah! Don't take me! Don't take me!"

Xiao Cheng, hiding behind her, seemed to be triggered by Li Mang’s murderous words and suddenly let out an even shriller scream.

He abruptly let go of Shen Li’s hem, completely losing his composure in his terror, and scrambled on his hands and feet, blindly diving under the table nearby.

"I don't live here! I don't know anything!"

His movements were so frantic and clumsy.

As he crawled under the table, his back slammed heavily against a table leg.

"Clang!"

The square table, crafted from fine pear wood, shook violently from the impact.

A blue-and-white porcelain brush washer on the table was not placed securely; it rolled off and shattered into pieces.

Even worse, a thick ledger that had been half-open, used to weigh down some papers on the corner of the table, lost its balance due to the violent shaking and slid off.

"Thud!"

The ledger hit the floor with a dull sound.

It did not close; instead, due to the impact, it flipped open a few more pages, landing right at Li Mang’s feet.

Everyone’s gaze was drawn to this sudden turn of events.

Li Mang subconsciously looked down.

He saw that the open ledger was clearly recording rows of entries in meticulous small-script calligraphy.

"Seventh day of the third month, gift to the Eastern Palace: ten hu of South Sea pearls, three thousand taels of gold."

"Nineteenth day of the third month, withdrawal by the Eastern Palace: one hundred thousand taels of silver."

"First day of the fourth month, secret transfer by the Eastern Palace: twelve Yangzhou 'slender horses'..."

Beside the handwriting was a perfectly clear, exclusive private seal of the Crown Prince’s Eastern Palace!

The room fell silent instantly.

The ferocious grin on Li Mang’s face froze the moment he saw that glaring private seal.

The color drained from his face rapidly, and cold sweat broke out on his forehead.

This... this is...

The Yanyu Pavilion is actually the Crown Prince’s private property?!

Moreover, it was a ledger recording every single dirty deal made with the Eastern Palace!

This wasn't some "catching an adulterer in the act." This was clearly digging a grave for the Crown Prince!

Before he could even react to this earth-shattering turn of events, the "rice merchants," who had been trembling like quails just moments ago, suddenly knelt in unison as if by prior agreement, wailing and crying out to Li Mang.

"General, save us! General, please uphold justice for us!"

The middle-aged man who appeared to be their leader pointed at the ledger, his face covered in snot and tears.

"We aren't bandits at all! We are legitimate grain merchants!"

"It was the Crown Prince... it was the Crown Prince who forced us to privately resell the official grain allocated by the imperial court for the Northern Frontier here, exchange it for silver, and send it into the Eastern Palace!"

"This ledger is the evidence! They recorded every single transaction we made!"

"We were forced into this against our will! General!"

This "identification" left Li Mang’s head buzzing, his mind instantly going blank.

Private resale of official grain!

That was a capital crime equivalent to treason!

The soldiers of the Capital Garrison he had brought were also stunned into silence. They looked at each other, their hands gripping their swords beginning to tremble.

They had come under orders to arrest a debauched, good-for-nothing prince.

How, in the blink of an eye, had this turned into a crime scene uncovering the Crown Prince’s corruption, fencing of stolen goods, and illegal sale of official grain?

Li Mang felt dizzy and lightheaded.

The men he had brought were now all eyewitnesses to the Crown Prince’s crimes!

He... he had set the Crown Prince up!

"Nonsense! You are slandering him!" Li Mang roared, his voice harsh but lacking conviction as he instinctively moved to snatch the lethal ledger.

*Clang!*

A crisp sound of a blade being unsheathed rang out.

Shen Li had drawn her sword at some point.

She didn't point it at Li Mang; she simply rested the tip of the blade in front of the ledger, carving a clear line into the polished floor.

She said nothing.

But the meaning could not have been clearer.

Cross this line, and you die!

Li Mang’s movements froze.

He looked into Shen Li’s calm eyes and felt a sudden chill run down his spine.

He did not doubt for a moment that if he took one more step forward, this woman would truly cut his head off.

It was over. Everything was over.

Amidst this extreme chaos, a trembling hand gently tugged at the corner of Shen Li’s robe.

"W-Wife... let’s... let’s go quickly..."

Xiao Cheng had crawled out from under the table at some point. His face was still streaked with tears, deathly pale, and his voice was shaking uncontrollably.

"It’s... it’s too scary here... I’m afraid..."

He pulled at Shen Li, wanting to leave, as if he didn't want to stay for even another second.

Shen Li followed him, her steps somewhat unsteady.

She looked back, taking a deep look at the scene of utter chaos.

She looked at the pale-faced Li Mang.

She looked at the ledger on the ground, enough to topple the Eastern Palace.

She looked at the "rice merchants" who were still wailing and "testifying" against the Crown Prince.

Finally, her gaze fell upon the man in front of her, who was still "trembling with fear" and pulling her away.

Coincidence?

Was all of this really just a coincidence?

From the golden medallion that "accidentally" fell at the Treasure Pavilion, to the ledger that was "accidentally" knocked out from under the table just now...

Every time, at the most desperate moment, he had snatched victory from the jaws of defeat through an incredible coincidence.

Every time, he had driven his opponent to ruin.

And yet, he—the good-for-nothing in everyone’s eyes—could always play the role of the most innocent, panicked, and helpless person in need of protection.

Shen Li suddenly felt a chill, her hair standing on end!

She looked at Xiao Cheng’s face, which was still plastered with "cowardice" and "fear."

For the first time, she felt a sense of... dread.

chapters.title: Exile to Cangbei
chapters.content:
That night at the Yanyu Pavilion turned the capital upside down.

Li Mang, Commander of the Capital Garrison, along with the lethal ledger, was "escorted" by Shen Li’s personal guards and sent into the palace in the dead of night.

The lights in the Emperor’s study, the Imperial Study, did not go out all night.

No one knew the extent of the thunderous rage of the sovereign on the dragon throne that night. They only knew that Crown Prince Xiao Rui knelt outside the Imperial Study for the entire night, and was only allowed inside when the dawn began to break.

When he emerged, his face was ashen, his spirit shattered.

Day had broken.

A storm that would sweep through the entire imperial court had officially begun.

The Taihe Hall.

Civil and military officials stood on both sides, the atmosphere stiflingly oppressive.

Everyone kept their heads low, eyes fixed on their noses, not daring to even breathe loudly.

On the dragon throne, Emperor Xiao Yuan looked grim, scrutinizing the Crown Prince kneeling below, and beside him, the cowering, huddled form of Xiao Cheng.

"Investigate!"

The Emperor’s voice was not loud, but it carried an indisputable majesty.

"The Yanyu Pavilion—investigate it for me! Investigate it to the very end!"

"Anyone involved, regardless of their rank, shall be punished without leniency!"

As soon as these words were spoken, several officials in the court felt their legs go weak, barely able to stand.

The Crown Prince kowtowed incessantly, his voice trembling: "Father, please calm your anger! This son... this son was merely confused for a moment, deceived by treacherous villains..."

"Confused?" The Emperor sneered, slamming a memorial onto the floor in front of the Crown Prince.

"Setting up private businesses, colluding with court officials, reselling official grain! Xiao Rui, is this what you call being confused?!"

"I entrusted you with the heavy responsibility of the heir to the nation—was it for you to use such methods to line your own pockets and form cliques for personal gain?!"

Every word struck the Crown Prince’s heart like a hammer.

Terrified out of his wits, the Crown Prince scrambled to defend himself: "Father, please see the truth! This son is wronged! This son knew nothing of the resale of official grain! It must be... it must be the manager of the Yanyu Pavilion, using this son’s name to swindle people outside!"

He spoke with such sincerity that it seemed as if he had suffered a great injustice.

Many officials from the Eastern Palace faction also stepped forward to defend the Crown Prince.

For a time, the court was in an uproar.

Just then, Xiao Cheng, who had been kneeling to the side as if scared out of his wits, suddenly let out a faint sob.

In the noisy hall, this sob should not have drawn attention.

Yet, for some reason, it caused everyone’s arguing to pause.

The Emperor’s gaze shifted from the Crown Prince to this son who had the least presence.

Xiao Cheng was kneeling on the cold gold-tiled floor, shaking uncontrollably, his face covered in tears and snot. The miserable and spineless sight of him was an eyesore to everyone.

"Father... Father, please spare me..." he sobbed while kowtowing. "This son... this son will never dare again... this son will never go to such places to cause trouble again..."

"It is all this son’s fault. I have brought shame upon the Imperial family and caused trouble for my elder brother... I beg Father to punish me alone, do not... do not vent your anger on my brother..."

His "sincere" crying and pleading ignited another fuse in the Emperor’s heart.

That’s right.

Wasn't the root cause of all this that this good-for-nothing went to the Yanyu Pavilion to "catch an adulterer"?

If he hadn't caused such a massive scene, even if the Crown Prince had many secrets, how could they have been exposed so embarrassingly in broad daylight?

Looking at Xiao Cheng, who was like mud that couldn't be plastered onto a wall, the Emperor’s anger found a perfect outlet.

"Enough!"

He slammed his hand onto the armrest of the dragon throne with a loud *bang*!

The entire hall fell silent instantly.

"An heir to the throne, unable to judge people and failing to govern his subordinates, nearly causing a catastrophe!"

"A prince, lacking ambition and causing trouble, stirring up a storm in the capital!"

The Emperor’s cold gaze swept back and forth between the Crown Prince and Xiao Cheng.

"My sons are truly impressive!"

Everyone held their breath, waiting for the Emperor’s final verdict.

"Crown Prince Xiao Rui, confined to the Eastern Palace for three months to reflect on your mistakes! Half of your ceremonial guards and expenses shall be stripped as a warning to others!"

This punishment could be considered neither light nor heavy.

It preserved the dignity of the heir while serving as a stern reprimand.

Upon hearing this, the Crown Prince felt as if he had been granted an amnesty, and he kowtowed to thank the Emperor: "This son... accepts the decree and thanks you!"

The officials of the Eastern Palace faction also breathed a sigh of relief.

Immediately after, the Emperor’s sharp gaze landed on Xiao Cheng.

"As for you..."

Xiao Cheng’s body shuddered violently, and he began to cry even harder.

The Emperor looked at his spineless appearance, making no effort to hide the disgust in his eyes.

"Seventh Prince Xiao Cheng, of poor character and incorrigible, is truly no blessing to the Imperial family!"

"I hereby issue a decree: you are to be exiled to your northern fief—Cangbei! Depart today, and you shall never return to the capital for as long as you live!"

As soon as this decree was issued, the entire court was in an uproar!

Cangbei!

What kind of place was that?

The northernmost, most barren, and most bitter cold fief of the Great Zhou!

It was plagued by snow year-round, the land was infertile, and the people lived in hardship. Even worse, Cangbei bordered the Northern Barbarians, and the border was constantly raided by barbarian cavalry, with bandits running rampant.

Let alone a pampered prince, even if a fierce general were sent there, he might not fare well!

Exiling Xiao Cheng there was no different from passing a death sentence.

The officials of the Crown Prince’s faction wore expressions of schadenfreude.

They knew that this Seventh Prince was completely finished for the rest of his life.

"Your Majesty, please reconsider!"

Just then, a very steady voice rang out from the ranks of the military officials.

Duke of Zhen, Shen Wei!

He wore purple official robes, his hair and beard were white, but his back was straight as a rod. His cloudy old eyes flashed with sharp light, commanding respect without anger.

As the foremost figure in the Great Zhou military, his words carried immense weight.

"Your Majesty, the Seventh Prince is mischievous and indeed deserves punishment. But Cangbei is a place of bitter cold, bordering the barbarians, and is extremely dangerous."

"My daughter, Shen Li, has just married into the Prince’s residence and is now to be sent to the frontier with her husband. In terms of both reason and sentiment... it is too harsh."

He did not plead for Xiao Cheng, but every word centered on his daughter.

The Emperor looked at this old general who had rendered great service to the Great Zhou, his expression softening slightly, yet his tone remained firm as iron.

"The Duke need not say more."

"A wife follows her husband; it is the natural order of things. Since she is the Princess of Xiao Cheng, she must naturally share in his joys and sorrows."

"On this matter, my mind is made up. A sovereign’s word is final!"

"A sovereign’s word is final."

These four words choked off everything Shen Wei had intended to say.

Shen Wei looked at the emperor on the dragon throne, whose resolve was set, and could only heave a long sigh before retreating back into the ranks.

He knew that to continue would not only fail to change the outcome but would instead invite the emperor’s suspicion.

And it was at this moment that the protagonist of this storm, Xiao Cheng, performed the most brilliant act of his life.

"Father! No, Father!"

He finally reacted to what he was about to face, letting out a wail as he scrambled forward, throwing himself at the emperor’s feet and clutching his legs.

"This son knows he was wrong! This son will never dare do it again! I beg you to retract your decree!"

"This son does not want to go to Cangbei! People die there! This son does not want to die!"

He wept until snot and tears streamed down his face, smearing them all over the emperor’s gold-embroidered dragon robe, perfectly portraying the despair, fear, and helplessness of a good-for-nothing.

The civil and military officials looked at his unsightly display with eyes full of contempt and disdain.

Even the Crown Prince revealed a cruel smile.

Go on, go to that hellhole of Cangbei and wither away.

No one saw that the moment Xiao Cheng buried his face in the emperor’s robe, his eyes, blurred by tears, erupted with wild ecstasy.

Ten years!

Ten whole years!

He had gone from an unfavored prince to a universally known waste.

He had endured all the mockery, humiliation, and cold shoulders.

He had fawned and groveled, clinging to life.

And for what?

For this very day!

The capital was a cage made of gold, a den of tigers and dragons! Here, he could only ever be the spineless, seventh-prince waste that everyone manipulated.

Only by leaving this place, by heading to that chaotic land ignored by all, a land full of opportunity, could he truly spread his wings!

The sky is vast for birds to fly, and the sea is wide for fish to leap!

Father, my good Father, you have personally opened the door to my cage!

His heart was ecstatic, yet on the surface, he remained the pathetic waste, clinging to the emperor’s leg and weeping as if his life depended on it.

In the end, it took two eunuchs, using all their might, to "tear" him away from the emperor’s leg and drag him to the side.

The imperial decree was officially issued.

Shen Li, dressed in her court attire, stood at the front of the military ranks. From beginning to end, she had not said a word, her expression not changing in the slightest; she was stone-faced.

When the eunuch handed the bright yellow scroll containing the decree of exile to her and Xiao Cheng, she accepted it without a flicker of emotion.

Beside her, Xiao Cheng was still sobbing softly in "heartbroken" despair.

Shen Li turned her head coldly, looking at his slightly trembling shoulders and his face twisted by "grief."

She leaned slowly toward his ear and, in a voice only the two of them could hear, said word by word:

"Cut the act."

"It’s disgusting."

chapters.title: Emptying Half the National Treasury
chapters.content:
Since receiving the decree at the Hall of Supreme Harmony, a bone-chilling cold had enveloped the Prince Cheng manor.

The emperor’s decree had spread throughout the capital, causing a massive uproar. Everyone knew that this Seventh Prince, who held the title of a prince but was in reality good for nothing, was finished for life.

Being banished to the godforsaken wasteland of Cangbei was no different from a death sentence; it was merely a slower, more painful way to die.

Servants packed their belongings, each face revealing a numb despair. Most of them had been assigned by the palace; following their master to Cangbei was like following him to his death, and the road ahead was bleak.

Shen Li paid them no mind.

She was alone in the training grounds, wiping her blade over and over again. The blade reflected her cold face, and deep within those phoenix eyes lay chaos.

"Cut the act. It’s disgusting."

The words she had spoken to him outside the Hall of Supreme Harmony had failed to move him in the slightest.

That man, her husband, Xiao Cheng, had merely stiffened for a moment before returning to his "heartbroken" state, sobbing all the way back to the manor, where he locked himself in his study and did not appear again.

He was unfathomable.

Just when you thought you had seen through him, peeling back one layer, you found an even thicker, deeper unknown beneath.

His composure when discussing the fate of the empire, his ruthlessness in diverting disaster onto others, and his acting skills in the court—turning black into white—all told Shen Li that this man was definitely not the waste he appeared to be.

Yet, he insisted on wrapping himself tightly in that most nauseating shell of cowardice.

It made her feel a surge of irritation.

This feeling was more suffocating than being surrounded by a hundred thousand troops on the battlefield.

"Princess." The voice of the captain of her personal guards, Uncle Zhang, came from behind, carrying a hint of heaviness. "People from the Ministry of Revenue are here. They say they are acting on the decree to issue the ceremonial guard and travel expenses for the trip to Cangbei. They ask for you and the Prince to come and verify the items."

Shen Li sheathed her sword and stood up.

"Where is he?"

"The Prince... is still in the study, saying he is too ashamed to see anyone." Uncle Zhang’s tone was difficult to describe.

Shen Li snorted coldly, said nothing more, and walked straight toward the front hall.

She wanted to see what new tricks that mad dog—the Crown Prince, whose face had been slapped swollen—could possibly play.

In the front hall, several minor officials in the robes of the Ministry of Revenue were sitting brazenly on chairs, drinking tea. The leader was the nephew of the Vice Minister of Revenue, surnamed Wang, who was usually a sycophant of the Crown Prince.

Seeing Shen Li enter, he didn't even bother to stand, merely cupping his hands with a mocking smile.

"This official greets the Princess. Where is the Prince? We are about to set off, so why is he still hiding? Could it be that he is afraid?"

The minor officials behind him let out a burst of suppressed snickers.

Shen Li’s gaze swept coldly over him.

The Vice Minister’s nephew felt a chill at her look, but thinking of the Crown Prince backing him, his courage returned. He pulled a list from his robes and slapped it lazily onto the table.

"Princess, this is the carriage, horses, and travel funds prepared for the Prince according to the imperial will. Please take a look."

Shen Li did not look at the paper; her gaze fell directly on the items parked in the courtyard.

The so-called "ceremonial guard" consisted of three dilapidated flatbed carts that were nearly falling apart, their wheels still caked in wet mud, as if dragged from some swamp.

The so-called "provisions" were a few bags of moldy, aged rice.

And as for the "travel funds," the Vice Minister’s nephew tapped a shriveled money bag at his waist, which emitted a hollow sound.

"Princess, you know how tight the national treasury is, and with the war in the south, we really... cannot spare any more. His Highness the Crown Prince said that the Seventh Prince is going to reflect on his mistakes, not to enjoy himself, so everything should be kept simple. I hope the Princess understands."

Though he spoke of "understanding," the mockery and schadenfreude on his face were undisguised.

Was this a ceremonial guard?

With these broken carts and this meager ration, let alone reaching Cangbei thousands of miles away, they wouldn't even make it three hundred miles outside the capital before being picked clean by bandits!

Uncle Zhang and the others behind Shen Li were livid, their hands already resting on their sword hilts.

"Insolence!" Uncle Zhang roared. "You are playing with human lives!"

"Hey, Captain Zhang, you can't say it like that." The Vice Minister’s nephew laughed fearlessly. "We are acting under orders. The list is written clearly; the Emperor only said to let the Seventh Prince go to his fief, he didn't say how much of a guard to provide. If you are dissatisfied, you are welcome to go argue with the Emperor."

He was certain that Shen Li would not dare.

The Emperor was currently in a rage; whoever touched this hornet's nest was courting death.

Murderous intent surged in Shen Li’s eyes.

She truly wanted to kill. Killing this clown before her would be easier than crushing an ant.

But she couldn't.

If she acted, the Crown Prince would immediately use the excuse of "publicly harming a court official" to force the Emperor to issue a decree, dragging the entire Duke of the State’s manor down with them.

That was exactly what they wanted.

Just as the tension reached its breaking point:

"Enough... don't... don't make things difficult for them..."

A cowardly voice came from outside the hall.

Everyone turned to see that Xiao Cheng had appeared. His eyes were red and swollen, his face haggard, looking like a man just recovered from a serious illness. He looked at the broken carts in the courtyard, then at the arrogant minor officials, a flash of humiliation and fear crossing his eyes, which eventually settled into resignation.

He walked up to the Vice Minister’s nephew and bowed deeply.

"Thank you... thank you, officials. We... we will accept these."

With trembling hands, he picked up the list full of insults, which felt heavy as lead.

Seeing his spineless display, the Vice Minister’s nephew laughed even more triumphantly.

"You’re a sensible one." He patted Xiao Cheng on the shoulder, his tone flippant. "Seventh Prince, travel slowly. The road to the underworld is slippery; be careful not to fall!"

With that, he took his men and walked away, laughing loudly.

"Your Highness!" Uncle Zhang’s eyes were bloodshot with rage. "How could you..."

"Forget it." Xiao Cheng interrupted him, his voice full of exhaustion and despair. "We... we cannot fight them."

He turned to look at Shen Li, forcing a smile that was uglier than crying.

"Princess... I have wronged you."

Shen Li did not speak; she just stared at him fixedly. Looking at his face, which was plastered with "resignation" and "incompetence," a nameless fire burned in her chest.

She did not fear death; she did not fear facing a thousand armies.

What she feared was this feeling of being throttled, unable to fight back!

And the man before her was the root of this frustration!

"Let's go," she spat out coldly.

"Go... go where?" Xiao Cheng was stunned.

"The Duke of the State’s manor."
