The carriage stopped in front of the Duke of the State’s manor.

The atmosphere inside was even more oppressive than at the Prince Cheng manor.

Shen Li’s father, the Duke of the State, Shen Wei, sat in the main seat in his casual robes, his face extremely grim.

Seeing his daughter and this "useless" son-in-law enter, a flash of anger crossed his eyes, which eventually melted into a heavy sigh.

"Father." Shen Li gave him a military salute.

"Father... Father-in-law..." Xiao Cheng knelt down with a thud, holding the shabby list high above his head.

Then, he wept.

He began to wail.

“Father-in-law, your son-in-law has failed you! And I have failed the Princess even more!”

As he wept, he slammed his head against the cold floor tiles, creating a rhythmic thudding sound.

“I am incompetent, I am a good-for-nothing. It wouldn’t matter if I died, but... but I cannot drag the Princess down to her death with me!”

“The Ministry of Revenue has gone too far! They are... they are leaving the Princess with no way to live, and leaving your Duke of Zhen’s estate with no way to survive!”

“I cannot protect the Princess, and I deserve to die for my incompetence. I beg you, Father-in-law, for the sake of the Princess, allow me... allow me to write a letter of divorce and set her free. My life is of no consequence! I absolutely cannot... I cannot let the Pearl of the Shen family be tarnished by the hands of a good-for-nothing like me!”

This tearful plea was truly heart-wrenching and sounded deeply sincere.

He took all the blame upon himself, never failing to mention that he was a good-for-nothing, yet every word was designed to fan the flames, elevating the Ministry of Revenue’s harassment into a direct provocation and conspiracy against Shen Li and the entire Duke of Zhen’s estate.

That final line about “writing a letter of divorce” was a stroke of genius.

Once these words were spoken, not only Shen Wei but even Shen Li, who stood to the side watching with cold eyes, felt a sudden jolt in her heart!

Divorce his wife?

A marriage bestowed by the Emperor—how could he just divorce her as he pleased?

By saying this, he would only make the Emperor believe he was defying an imperial decree and slapping the face of the Imperial family! When the thunderous wrath of the Emperor descended, it would only be more violent!

Shen Wei had spent his whole life on the battlefield; what kind of people had he not seen? How could he fail to see through Xiao Cheng’s clumsy acting?

But he didn't care!

Every word Xiao Cheng spoke hit home.

He might not care about the life or death of this useless son-in-law, but he could not be indifferent to the safety of his own daughter!

Bullying his, Shen Wei’s, daughter? Did they think his thirty thousand Northern Frontier troops were just for show?

“Enough!”

Shen Wei slammed his hand onto the table, and the desk, crafted from a single piece of ironwood, actually cracked under the force.

He stood up abruptly, his hulking frame towering over the room.

“They have gone too far!”

A terrifying murderous aura erupted from the old Duke’s eyes.

“Do they really think that I, Shen Wei, am old and can no longer lift a blade?”

Without even glancing at Xiao Cheng, who was still “weeping bitterly” on the floor, he strode out, roaring, “Someone, ready my horse!”

“Father!” Shen Li was startled and quickly stepped forward to stop him. “Where are you going? You cannot go to the Ministry of Revenue; this is the Crown Prince’s trap!”

“The Ministry of Revenue?” Shen Wei sneered, a sharpness unique to an old veteran flashing in his eyes.

“Who said I was going to that place where pedantic scholars dwell?”

“Don’t they complain that the national treasury is empty? Fine! I, Shen Wei, will go and take what I need myself!”

The old Duke donned the heavy Qilin armor that symbolized the soul of the Great Zhou military. He vaulted onto his horse, not carrying a blade, but holding a token that had long been gathering dust while enshrined in the ancestral hall.

It was the token bestowed by the late Emperor: *As if the Emperor himself were present!*

He took no soldiers, riding alone at full gallop toward the Ministry of War!

At the Ministry of War, the Minister and several Vice Ministers were in the middle of a meeting when they heard the Duke of Zhen had arrived in full armor. Terrified, they rushed out to welcome him.

They watched as the old Duke dismounted, said nothing, and marched straight into the Ministry’s archive room.

Under their bewildered and anxious gazes, he pulled a yellowed, ox-hide-wrapped ancestral scroll from the highest, dust-covered shelf.

He unfurled the scroll and pressed the late Emperor’s token heavily upon it!

Then, with a voice that could shake the entire capital, he read out, word for word:

“Great Zhou Ancestral Code, Volume Three, Article Seven!”

“Any legitimate daughter of the Duke of Zhen, when accompanying her husband to guard the border, shall have an honor guard equivalent to a Princess on tour! She may use the late Emperor’s military tally to requisition ‘Princess-level’ military equipment and supplies from the Ministry of War’s armory!”

“Minister of War, receive the decree!”

Once these words were spoken, the entire Ministry of War fell deathly silent!

Everyone was stunned by this ancestral rule, long forgotten in the dust of history!

Princess-level military equipment—what kind of concept was that?

Overnight, the scene in front of Prince Cheng’s residence changed completely.

The three dilapidated flatbed carts were replaced by over a dozen sturdy war chariots capable of deflecting arrows!

The few bags of moldy, stale rice were replaced by hundreds of crates neatly stacked with military-grade dried meat and wheat cakes!

And most chilling of all were the guards.

There were no imperial guards, no private retainers.

There were three hundred battle-hardened elites who had retired from the Northern Frontier. They wore uniform black armor and stood silently beside the chariots, each exuding a thick scent of blood. Their eyes were cold and numb; killing had become an instinct.

This was no exile! This was clearly a small, heavily armed expeditionary force!

When the news reached the Eastern Palace, Crown Prince Xiao Rui shattered his favorite jade vase on the spot. He was so angry he nearly vomited blood, yet he couldn't say a single word!

The ancestral code and the military tally.

These were ironclad laws that even his Imperial Father could not refute! He could only watch helplessly as Xiao Cheng emptied nearly a quarter’s worth of the Ministry of War’s supplies and prepared to leave the city in a grand procession.

That night, at Prince Cheng’s residence.

Shen Li stood in the courtyard, looking at the brand-new, menacing convoy, her heart filled with a complex mix of emotions.

She turned back to look at the man standing in the shadow of the veranda pillar.

He had changed out of his plain clothes and was looking down, adjusting his cuffs. The sorrow of the day was gone, replaced by a calm that bordered on indifference.

He seemed to sense her gaze, slowly looked up, and offered her a smile.

The smile was faint, but it was no longer fawning or cowardly.

“Princess,” his voice had also returned to a strange, steady composure, “the road should be safe now.”

“We can set off with peace of mind.”

chapters.title: Just Right for Drilling Troops
chapters.content:
The convoy set off.

It was a highly incongruous procession.

On the perimeter were three hundred elite Northern Frontier soldiers clad in black armor. Each of them exuded the blood-scent of long-term battlefield service, their eyes scanning the surroundings for any sign of movement.

Wherever this force went, mountain bandits and roving outlaws would flee at the mere sight of them.

Yet, the core of this force was completely at odds with this murderous atmosphere.

In the most luxurious and heavily guarded carriage sat their master, Prince Cheng, Xiao Cheng.

Since leaving the capital, the Prince had not shown his face once.

The carriage curtains remained tightly drawn, as if he were isolating himself from everything outside. His daily meals were delivered to the carriage by a designated person, and he would retrieve them himself. Aside from the occasional muffled, terrified gasp heard when the carriage hit a bump, there was a deathly silence inside, devoid of any vitality.

Shen Li rode at the very front of the convoy.

She had become completely numb to the man in the carriage.

In the few days since leaving the capital, she had thought a lot.

The scene at the Yanyu Pavilion was deeply etched in her mind. Was that Xiao Cheng—the man who pointed out the state of the world with such steady composure—real, or was it a hallucination?

But whenever she tried to probe, the man would immediately revert to that cowardly persona that made her feel nauseated.

He was like a top-tier actor, playing the role of a “good-for-nothing” to perfection. And she was the audience member being led around by the nose.

This feeling made her very uncomfortable.

But what made her even more irritable was what her father had told her before she left.

“Li’er, the Emperor bestowed you upon the Seventh Prince and set his fief in Cangbei. His intent is not the Prince, but our Shen family.”

“Cangbei is the throat of my Northern Frontier army. The Emperor wants to use this marriage to bind our Shen family’s hands and feet to the imperial power.”

“Whether Xiao Cheng is a good-for-nothing or a great leader, it doesn’t matter. What matters is that he is your husband. Protecting him is protecting the Shen family. You must remember this.”

Therefore, no matter how pathetic the man was, she had to ensure his safety.

This was her responsibility, and her shackle.

“Princess!”

A scout in the guise of a personal guard galloped toward her from the front, his expression grave.

“Thirty miles ahead is the ‘Yixiantian’ gorge. Our scouts discovered signs of a large number of horse bandits operating there. There are at least five hundred of them!”

At these words, the pace of the convoy slowed.

The captain of the guards, Uncle Zhang, rode up to Shen Li, his brow furrowed.

“My Lady, Yixiantian is a treacherous place, easy to defend and hard to attack. If five hundred bandits hold that position, even if we manage to break through, we will suffer heavy losses. Not to mention, we still have to protect the Prince and all these supplies.”

“Should we take a detour? If we go fifty miles west, there is a small path. It’s harder to travel, but we can bypass Yixiantian.”

Uncle Zhang’s suggestion was the cautious, experienced advice.

Shen Li pulled on her reins, gazing at the silhouette of the gorge in the distance, which looked like the gaping maw of a giant beast. A spark of battle-lust ignited in her phoenix eyes.

Horse bandits?

Near the capital, under the Emperor’s very nose, where would five hundred horse bandits come from, and who would dare ambush a royal convoy?

One didn't need to think twice to know it was that mad dog, the Crown Prince, who wouldn't give up!

He wanted her to die on the road?

Fine.

Then let’s see whose blade is harder!

“No need to detour,” Shen Li’s voice was cold and resolute. “A mere five hundred petty thieves are not worthy of making me, Shen Li, flee in fear.”

“Pass my order: the entire army is to form up, adopt the arrowhead formation, and prepare to charge!”

The three hundred elites behind her, upon hearing this, showed no fear; instead, their eyes gleamed with bloodthirsty excitement. They were wolves, tigers—what they craved most was to tear out the enemy’s throat!

“My Lady, you cannot!” Uncle Zhang was anxious. “We are at a numerical disadvantage, and we are burdened by all these supplies. A frontal charge is too risky! The Prince’s safety...”

“I will be responsible for his safety,” Shen Li interrupted, her tone brooking no argument.

Just as she was about to order the full assault, a cowardly, trembling voice drifted out from the carriage.

“D-don’t fight...”

The curtain was lifted a crack, revealing Xiao Cheng’s deathly pale face.

“Are there... are there bandits outside? H-how many?”

Shen Li looked at his terrified expression, and the battle-lust in her heart was instantly extinguished, leaving only endless disgust.

“Five hundred,” she replied coldly.

"Five... five hundred?!" Xiao Cheng’s voice shifted pitch entirely, as if someone had grabbed him by the throat.

"Then... then why are we still fighting! Quick... run!" He was almost on the verge of tears. "I... I’ve thought of it! I’ve thought of a good plan!"

Clinging to it like a life-saving straw, he said urgently, "I... I was bored a few days ago and looked at an old map. I remember... I remember there is a very, very small path nearby that can bypass that 'First Line of Sky' place!"

"We... we should split our forces! Let... let a small squad light many torches, beat drums and gongs, and take the main road to lure all the bandits away! Then our main force can take... take me and all the gold and silver treasures and sneak through that small path! They definitely won't notice!"

"How about it? Princess, is... is my idea... is it very good?"

After he finished speaking, he looked at Shen Li with an expression full of anticipation, as if saying, "Praise me quickly."

The entire caravan fell silent at his words.

Even the disciplined Northern elite soldiers felt their lips twitching slightly.

Split the forces?

Use a small squad as bait to attract the attention of five hundred horse bandits?

How was that any different from sending them to their deaths?

And the main force would just sneak away with the gold, silver, and this useless Prince?

This idea...

It was cowardly to the extreme and shameless to the point of absurdity!

Uncle Zhang’s face turned beet red. He wanted to retort, but he didn't know where to begin. Because, from a certain "preserving the big picture" perspective, this seemingly most shameless method was actually the one with the least loss.

Shen Li stared fixedly at Xiao Cheng.

Looking at his cowardly, self-righteous face, she felt a surge of blood rise in her chest.

She had been on the battlefield for ten years and had never once considered fleeing in the face of battle.

Every soldier under her command was her brother-in-arms; she would never abandon a single one to serve as bait!

This was her bottom line; it was her honor!

Yet, the man before her had easily trampled her honor underfoot.

"Princess... why... why are you looking at me like that..." Xiao Cheng felt a chill from her gaze and shrank back into the carriage. "I... I am doing this for everyone's safety... as the saying goes, 'as long as the green hills remain, there’s no need to worry about firewood'..."

"Shut up!" Shen Li barked sternly.

She whipped her horse around, refusing to look at that face which disgusted her.

Her heart was in a state of violent struggle.

Reason told her that although Xiao Cheng’s plan was shameless, it was the safest. Protecting the supplies and the safety of this good-for-nothing was her father’s strict order.

But her instincts and her pride made it impossible for her to accept such a way of abandoning her comrades to save her own skin.

Time ticked away.

In the distance, the entrance to the canyon was pitch black and unnaturally quiet, waiting for them to step inside.

In the end, reason overcame pride.

Shen Li slowly closed her eyes, and when she opened them again, her gaze had become cold and resolute.

"Uncle Zhang."

"The subordinate is here!"

"You, take fifty men and go by the main road." Shen Li’s voice was somewhat hoarse. "Make as much noise as possible."

Uncle Zhang’s body jolted, his eyes filled with absolute disbelief, but in an instant, that shock transformed into the absolute obedience of a soldier. He didn't ask a single word, only cupped his hands heavily: "Yes!"

"Wait!" Shen Li stopped him, dismounted, and took a small but sturdy leather pouch from her personal bag. Inside were the few types of gold-wound medicine and life-saving pills she cherished most. She stuffed it into Uncle Zhang’s arms and unbuckled the personal dagger from her waist—a blade that could cut through iron like mud—and handed it to him as well.

"Tell the brothers," she said, staring into Uncle Zhang’s eyes, word by word, "this is not going to die; it is to distract the enemy. Do everything in your power to survive. In one hour, I will personally lead men back to support you! This is a military order!"

No one moved.

Three hundred men stood like three hundred statues, motionless.

"Good!" Uncle Zhang smiled with gratification. "Since no one is afraid of death, then I shall personally select the men!"

He picked out fifty of the most elite veterans—men who had crawled out of piles of corpses with him.

Those whose names were called showed no fear; instead, they puffed out their chests, as if this were an honor.

"Princess," Uncle Zhang looked at Shen Li one last time, his eyes resolute, "if this subordinate does not return, I entrust the remaining brothers to you!"

With that, he took those fifty soldiers, grabbed a large number of torches and spare military drums from the supply wagons, and marched toward the First Line of Sky without hesitation.

There was no sense of tragedy in their movements; their steps were firm, and some even began to hum the war songs of the Northern Territory in low voices.

The singing was desolate and powerful.

Watching their determined backs as they left, the remaining two hundred and fifty soldiers silently lowered their heads.

Shen Li’s fingernails were deeply embedded in her palms.

She had never felt so humiliated.

"Pr... Princess, let... let us go quickly too." Xiao Cheng’s urging voice came from the carriage again.

Shen Li did not answer.

She used all her strength to kick her horse’s flanks hard!

"Giddyap!"

The warhorse neighed and carried her, without looking back, galloping toward the unknown small path.

The main force, led by her, followed in silence and soon disappeared into the rugged mountain forest.

On the other side.

The First Line of Sky canyon.

The leader of the private soldiers sent by the Crown Prince was lying on the cliff, waiting anxiously.

"Boss, why haven't they come yet? They didn't run away, did they?"

"Shut up!" the leader cursed impatiently. "The scout said they only have one road to take! With such heavy supplies, they can't run fast! Keep your eyes peeled!"

Just then, a sentry came scrambling over.

"Boss! They’re here! They’re here!"

"They’re here!"

The leader’s spirit lifted, and he quickly picked up his telescope to look toward the canyon entrance.

In the distance, a troop was beating drums and gongs, holding dozens of blazing torches, marching toward the canyon in a grand manner.

The momentum was as if they were afraid others wouldn't know they were coming.

The leader gave a cruel, sinister laugh.

Idiots!

Did they really think this was an outing in the suburbs of the capital?

"Pass my order!" He lowered his voice, his eyes full of greed. "Everyone, prepare to move!"

"As soon as they enter the canyon, fire arrows! Start the fires! Push all the rocks down for me!"

"Remember, His Highness the Crown Prince has ordered that the waste in the carriage must be kept alive! As for that woman..."

He licked his chapped lips.

"Try to keep her alive too! Brothers, whether we get promoted and rich depends on today!"

"Yes!"

The five hundred "horse bandits" responded in unison, all revealing bloodthirsty gazes.

They lurked in the shadows, their eyes greedy and fierce, waiting for the "fat sheep" to step, step by step, into this burial ground prepared for them.

chapters.title: The Princess Bathed in Blood
chapters.content:
First Line of Sky canyon.

The battle ended faster than imagined.

When the last "horse bandit" had his throat slit by Uncle Zhang’s blade and fell softly into a pool of blood, the battle-hardened veteran leaned on his sword, breathing heavily.

He looked around; of the original fifty brothers, fewer than thirty were still standing.

Everyone was wounded, and everyone’s armor was stained dark red with blood—it was impossible to tell if it was the enemy’s or their own.

At their feet lay layers of corpses.

They had won this ambush.

They won it tragically, and they won it... inexplicably.

"Boss Zhang," a young soldier said while bandaging a wound on his arm, looking confused, "these bastards, they looked so numerous, how were they so vulnerable when we fought? All thunder and no rain—aside from that first wave of arrows, they were just a bunch of rabble afterward!"

Uncle Zhang frowned as well.

Something was indeed wrong.

The enemy had five hundred men holding a strategic position, and they were attacking uphill; it should have been a life-or-death struggle.

But once they actually engaged, they realized that this group of so-called "horse bandits," aside from being well-equipped, had terrible tactical skills. Their formations were chaotic, they fought individually, and there was no coordination at all. They were just a group of temporarily assembled servants and guards, not true, hardened bandits.

They... were acting.

They were playing the role of "fierce" in an extremely clumsy way.

If not for that, his fifty men could never have wiped out an enemy ten times their size while only losing twenty-some lives.

"Clean the battlefield, count the casualties, and rest in place!" Uncle Zhang suppressed the doubts in his heart and ordered in a low voice, "Everyone, stay alert!"

He had a bad premonition.

This trap was too big. So big that every one of them was just a helpless pawn on a chessboard.

And the real killing blow was definitely not here.

...

Meanwhile, on that winding forest path.

The main force led by Shen Li was shrouded in a sudden shadow of death.

Dozens of assassins in black emerged like ghosts from the dense forest on both sides of the road without warning!

They moved swiftly, coordinated perfectly, and every move was a killing strike. Their goal was clear—not the supplies, not the guards, but the carriage in the very center of the troop, belonging to the Seventh Prince, Xiao Cheng!

"Assassins! Protect the Prince!"

The two hundred Northern soldiers left behind were elites, but their duty was primarily to guard the supplies, and their mental state was far less tense than Uncle Zhang’s "bait" squad.

Caught off guard, they were instantly thrown into chaos by these long-planned assassins!

The martial arts style of these assassins was completely different from the "horse bandits" at the First Line of Sky! They were more professional and more lethal. Every strike of their blades precisely pierced the throats and hearts of the guards. If they missed, they retreated immediately, never lingering in the fight.

In the blink of an eye, over a dozen guards had fallen in pools of blood.

The defensive line was torn wide open!

"Whoosh—!"

A sharp sound of something piercing the air tore through the chaotic battlefield!

A deep blue arrowhead pierced through the blind spot of the crowd, pinning itself directly into the window of the carriage where Xiao Cheng was!

On that arrow was a deadly poison that kills upon contact with blood!

This was the Crown Prince’s true trump card!

He had never expected that bunch of trash at Yixiantian to accomplish anything; those five hundred men were merely another "bait" used to distract Shen Li and force her to divide her forces!

From beginning to end, his target had only ever been Xiao Cheng!

By killing Xiao Cheng and framing it as a failure of protection by Shen Li’s guards, he could kill two birds with one stone: eliminate a thorn in his side while severely humiliating the Duke of the State’s mansion!

In a flash, Shen Li’s pupils contracted sharply!

She was still ten paces away from the carriage!

She saw the arrow clearly, saw its flight trajectory, and saw the deadly, dark blue hue upon it.

It was too late!

There was no time to think!

The instinct honed by years of warfare overcame everything else!

Protect the commander!

Even if this commander was a piece of trash!

"Hyah!"

Shen Li let out a furious roar and dug her heels hard into the horse’s flanks! The warhorse, in pain, let out a mournful neigh and reared up, using its hind legs as a pivot to execute an incredible lateral turn!

She did not draw her blade to parry, because she knew there wasn't enough time!

She chose the most direct, and also the most brutal, method.

She would use her own body to block it!

*Squelch!*

The sound of the sharp arrow piercing flesh was dull yet distinct.

The poison-tipped arrow pierced through Shen Li’s left shoulder blade from behind without the slightest suspense! The immense force carried her, slamming her hard against the wall of the carriage with a dull, heavy thud.

Blood instantly stained her armor red.

A pain deep into the marrow exploded!

Shen Li did not fall!

The excruciating pain instead ignited the most primal ferocity in her bones!

"Roar!"

She let out a roar, violently drew the saber at her waist with her right hand, and with a backhand strike, cleaved an assassin attempting to approach the carriage—man and blade alike—into two!

Warm blood splattered across her face.

She ignored it all. With the arrow still humming in her left shoulder, she fought with no regard for her own life, swinging her long saber and clearing a vacuum of death in front of the carriage!

The surrounding assassins were stunned by her fearless, death-defying display!

It was at this moment that the Black Armored Army, having finished off the enemies in front, arrived from the rear to provide support! They formed a battle array, acting like an efficient meat grinder, quickly surrounding, isolating, and slaughtering the remaining assassins!

The battle ended in a very short time.

The carriage curtain was ripped open by a trembling hand.

Xiao Cheng rushed out.

When he saw Shen Li, drenched in blood with the black arrow protruding from her shoulder, yet still standing tall, his pupils contracted violently in an instant!

All the expressions on that face, which always wore cowardice and terror, vanished in that moment!

It was an undisguised, explosive rage! It was the rage and agony of seeing a precious treasure damaged!

He subconsciously reached out, his hand passing through the air, wanting to touch the glaring fletching of the arrow in her shoulder.

His fingertips could even feel the scorching heat radiating from her wound.

However, his hand stopped dead just half an inch from her wound!

That outstretched hand suddenly clenched into a fist, the veins on the back of his hand bulging!

The next second, that cold, icy face was once again masked with that panicked, helpless expression.

Only this time, his performance carried a madness so real it was chilling!

"Military doctor! Military doctor!"

He turned his head and let out a heart-wrenching roar at the personal guards behind him!

"Call the military doctor quickly! The Princess Consort is injured! She’s injured!"

The voice was shrill and sharp, even cracking due to the extreme emotional fluctuation.

He rushed to Shen Li’s side, wanting to support her swaying body, but his hands were shaking so violently he dared not touch her.

"Princess Consort... Princess Consort, how are you... please don't scare me..."

His tears rolled down in large drops, falling onto Shen Li’s blood-stained armor.

Shen Li’s consciousness was already beginning to blur.

The dizziness from blood loss and the paralysis from the arrow poison were assaulting her nerves.

In the final moment before losing consciousness, she saw it.

She saw it clearly.

In that instant, the kind of explosive rage that flashed in Xiao Cheng’s eyes was something that absolutely did not belong to a piece of trash.

That was no disguise.

That was a kind of... truth from the depths of his soul.

Then, she saw his face switch instantly back to weeping and wailing.

Reality and falsehood overlapped crazily before her eyes.

This man... exactly what...

She could no longer hold on; her vision went black, and she lost consciousness completely, falling softly into a trembling yet firm embrace.

Xiao Cheng, holding her soft body, still wore an expression of inconsolable grief.

He raised his head, his eyes blurred by tears, looking past the crowd at Xuan Yi, the commander of the Black Armored Army who had hurried over.

That gaze was ice-cold, devoid of a shred of warmth.

Xuan Yi felt a chill in his heart and immediately knelt on one knee, lowering his head.

"My Lord, this subordinate has failed in his duty!"

"Trash."

Holding Shen Li, Xiao Cheng coldly spat out the word in a voice only the two of them could hear.

"I let you train the troops, not to let you ruin the edge of my blade!"

"I have noted this debt."

Xuan Yi buried his head lower, his body trembling slightly from fear.

Xiao Cheng stopped looking at him, and holding the unconscious woman in his arms, he turned toward the approaching military doctors and let out that sorrowful, anxious roar once more.

"What are you standing there for! Save her!"

"If she dies, I will have all of you buried with her!"

chapters.title: Three Birds with One Arrow
chapters.content: Pain, excruciating pain. Boundless, intense pain exploded in Shen Li’s left shoulder. Following that, waves of alternating heat and cold crashed against her consciousness, one after another. Scorching heat and icy cold ravaged her body in turns, tearing her apart in two extremes of torture. In the intervals of her昏沉 (drowsiness), countless chaotic images flashed before her eyes. The wind and snow of the Northern Frontier, the iron hooves of the battlefield, the shrill whistle of arrows piercing the air, and also... a pair of eyes. What kind of eyes were those? The moment she was struck by the arrow, those eyes, which were usually filled with cowardice and terror, erupted with a rage she had never seen before. That was not a disguise. That pain was as real as the wound on her shoulder at that moment. But the next second, those eyes were drowned in tears, switching back to the cowardice and helplessness she was most familiar with and most loathed. "Military doctor! Call the military doctor quickly!" "If she dies, I will have all of you buried with her!" That desperate, hoarse roar seemed to still echo in her ears. Was it acting, or was it real? Which one was the true him? Shen Li opened her eyes abruptly; the violent movement tugged at her wound, causing her to let out a muffled groan. What came into view was the ceiling of the tent, the air filled with the heavy scent of medicinal herbs and a faint smell of blood. "Princess Consort! You’re awake!" A voice filled with both shock and joy rang in her ears. Shen Li turned her head with difficulty and saw Xiao Cheng’s magnified, haggard, and worried face. There were dark circles under his eyes, blue stubble on his chin, and his black robes were wrinkled, looking as if he hadn't closed his eyes for days. Seeing her wake up, he hurriedly and clumsily picked up a bowl of warm medicinal soup from the side. "Quick... drink the medicine quickly. The military doctor said you were poisoned and have a high fever that won't subside; you must take the medicine on time..." He clumsily scooped up a spoonful of the dark brown liquid and brought it to Shen Li’s lips. Because his hand was shaking, a few drops of the scalding medicine spilled onto the back of his own hand, burning him so that he hissed, but he paid it no mind. Shen Li did not open her mouth. She simply stared at him with her phoenix eyes, which appeared exceptionally bright due to the high fever. "Those people..." her voice was hoarse from thirst, "...who were they?" Xiao Cheng’s action of feeding the medicine stiffened, and the expression on his face was somewhat blank: "What... what people?" "Those assassins," Shen Li’s gaze was as sharp as a blade, "and... those black-armored soldiers who appeared suddenly." The "bandits" of Yixiantian. The assassins on the forest path. And finally, the black-armored elites who suddenly appeared to surround and slaughter the assassins. These three groups of people definitely did not belong to the same side. Especially that last Black Armored Army; their battle formation and coordination were definitely not something ordinary guards could possess! They looked more like... a well-trained private army! "I... I don't know..." The blankness on Xiao Cheng’s face turned into terror, "I was so scared at the time, I didn't see anything clearly... I only saw you, Princess Consort... you were struck by an arrow to save me..." As he spoke, his eyes turned red again, and his voice carried a sobbing tone. "It’s all my fault, it’s all because I’m useless. If it weren't to protect a piece of trash like me, you wouldn't have..." "I am asking you, who were those people!" Shen Li interrupted his nauseating performance and used all her strength to ask, word by word. Her interrogation seemed to make Xiao Cheng even more flustered. "I... I really don't know... perhaps... perhaps they were people sent by Father to protect us in secret?" He seemed to think of something, his eyes lighting up, "Right! It must be that! Father-in-law must have been worried about us, so he sent people to follow! Look, Princess Consort, didn't those people kill the assassins later? They must have come to save us!" This explanation... It was seamless. Given her father, the Duke of the State’s power and his love for her, sending a secret elite force to protect her was reasonable. Even the three hundred elites previously moved out from the Ministry of War were assumed by everyone, including Shen Li herself, to be her father’s doing. Another team acting in secret seemed plausible. Shen Li looked at his smug, foolish face, and a wave of disgust rose in her chest. She wanted to refute it, but she couldn't find any flaws. The high fever and excruciating pain made it impossible for her to concentrate. She only felt her head splitting with pain, and in the end, she could only close her eyes and ignore him. Seeing that she stopped questioning, Xiao Cheng breathed a sigh of relief as if he had been granted an amnesty. He continued to clumsily feed her the medicine, spoonful by spoonful. The moment he turned to put down the medicine bowl, the cowardice and lingering fear on his face vanished without a trace. In their place was a cold, icy expression. With the corner of his eye, he glanced at the woman on the bed whose breathing was rapid, his fingers tapping lightly against his sleeve. Xuan Yi, who had been guarding outside the tent, paused imperceptibly before quietly withdrawing. A command had been silently issued. …… Shen Li lay in a coma for three days. During these three days, the entire caravan remained where it was, setting up camp without moving a single step further. Xiao Cheng stayed by her bedside, never leaving her side. He served tea, administered medicine, and wiped her body, doing everything himself. His "deep affection" and "self-reproach" were plain for all to see. The Shen family guards, who had previously looked down on this useless prince, began to view him with a subtle change in their eyes. And during these three days, an urgent report, marked for eight hundred li of travel, had been carried day and night by a death soldier of the Xuanjia Army to the capital, where it was presented on the Emperor’s desk. The content of the report was simple yet shocking. —"The Seventh Prince, Xiao Cheng, accompanied by his consort Shen Li, was ambushed by Northern Barbarian spies near Yixiantian while en route to his fief. To protect the Prince, Consort Shen Li fought at the vanguard, engaging the barbarians in a life-or-death struggle. She was struck by a poisoned arrow and remains in critical condition, having successfully ensured the safety of the Prince and the imperial military supplies." Once the news broke, the entire imperial court was shaken! Everyone knew tacitly that the Crown Prince had sent men to assassinate him, but that was, after all, a sordid affair that could not be brought into the light. But the moment the words "Northern Barbarian spies" were uttered, the nature of the matter changed entirely! This was no longer a struggle between princes; it was treason and selling out the country! In an instant, the entire court turned its focus toward the border generals who had murky ties with the Northern Barbarians, and... the Crown Prince’s faction, which had consistently advocated for peace talks with them! The Eastern Palace. "Clang!" Crown Prince Xiao Rui smashed the teacup in his hand against the floor, shattering it into pieces. "Northern Barbarian spies?!" He was trembling with rage, his face livid. "Good! A very good Xiao Cheng! A thief crying 'stop thief' indeed!" He had clearly sent his own trained death soldiers; how did they become Northern Barbarian spies? This was clearly that useless wretch Xiao Cheng turning the tables on him! Yet, he could not refute a single word! What could he say? That they weren't Northern Barbarian spies, but assassins he had sent to kill his own brother? He dared not! He could only watch helplessly as this bucket of filth was poured squarely over his head! Not only had he lost his wife and soldiers, suffering casualties, but he had also brought a scandal upon himself! In the imperial court, the pro-war officials, led by Duke of Zhen Shen Wei, were filled with righteous indignation. They submitted memorials one after another, demanding a thorough investigation into the matter and the severe punishment of those who had colluded with the enemy! Shen Wei even wept, declaring in court that his daughter had died for the country without regret, but if there were treacherous sycophants in the court colluding with the barbarians to harm loyal subjects, he would be the first to oppose them! For a time, the Shen family’s reputation did not fall but rose, reaching an unprecedented peak! And public opinion among the common people had completely reversed. Countless citizens and scholars were praising the "loyal and brave" deeds of the Seventh Princess, Shen Li. A woman, facing barbarian spies, had fought at the vanguard, bathed in blood, to protect her husband and the imperial supplies! What loyalty! What courage! In an instant, Shen Li became a heroine in the hearts of all the people of Great Zhou, a paragon of peerless loyalty and bravery. And the man she had protected with her life, Xiao Cheng, while still looked down upon, was now begrudgingly acknowledged by those who mocked him as a "useless wretch"—they had to admit he had married a good princess. All of this, as if it had grown wings, flew back to the caravan camp hundreds of miles away. When Shen Li finally woke from her high fever and was able to walk, these were the "praises" she heard, which left her between laughter and tears. She had become a hero. A loyal, brave, and peerless heroine celebrated by the world. She stood at the entrance of the tent, listening to the soldiers nearby discussing her with pride, and found it incredibly ironic. Loyal and brave? She was merely... used as a blade, a shield, and a pawn by the man she looked down upon the most. She had paid with real blood and pain, yet she had secured a perfect political victory for him. He had not only shed his skin like a cicada to escape the Crown Prince's subsequent pursuit, but he had also dumped this bucket of filth squarely onto the Crown Prince's head, leaving him unable to speak of his grievances. And in the process, he had earned immense fame and prestige for her and the Shen family. Three birds with one stone. A fine calculation. Truly... a fine calculation! "Princess, why have you come out? It's windy outside, go back and rest!" Xiao Cheng’s voice rang out at the perfect moment. He walked over quickly with a thick cloak, intending to drape it over her. His face still wore that expression of deep concern and lingering fear. Shen Li did not move. She simply looked at him quietly, looking into those eyes filled with "worry." Behind that worry, she could almost see a cold, calculating mind. She slowly raised her hand, not reaching for the cloak. Under Xiao Cheng’s startled gaze, she used the last bit of strength she had just recovered to grab his wrist! That wrist, seemingly slender, was as hard as iron. The "worry" on Xiao Cheng’s face showed a slight stiffness the moment she grabbed him. Shen Li stared at him, her phoenix eyes, which had once weathered the storms of the Northern Frontier, now holding only cold, undisguised scrutiny. She asked clearly, word for word: "Xiao Cheng, who exactly are you?" *** **Chapter 11: You ask who I am? I'm just a useless wretch who loves his princess!** "Xiao Cheng, who exactly are you?" Shen Li’s voice was very soft, carrying a trace of imperceptible hoarseness due to the fever and pain. But every word carried an unquestionable weight. The hand gripping his wrist didn't use much strength; the sharp pain in her left shoulder prevented her from exerting force. Yet, Xiao Cheng stiffened as if he had been burned by a red-hot iron. The concern and worry on his face appeared to have cracks, like the surface of a frozen lake. Beneath those cracks lay the deep, bottomless cold and calculation that Shen Li was all too familiar with. Although it lasted only for an instant, so fast it felt like an illusion, Shen Li had seen it clearly. It was these eyes! At the Yanyu Pavilion, on the forest path, the moment she blocked the poisoned arrow for him—it was these same eyes! One side was an abyss, and the other was the disgusting duckweed floating upon it. The wrist she held, seemingly slender, was actually as hard as iron; the muscles beneath his long gown were taut like a drawn bowstring. This was a reaction only someone who had practiced martial arts for years would have. All the clues, all the suspicions, converged at this moment into a giant net, firmly trapping Xiao Cheng. Shen Li’s gaze was as sharp as a knife, intending to peel away his disguises layer by layer to see his true face. However, just as she thought she was about to touch the truth— The coldness and stiffness in Xiao Cheng’s eyes melted away like snow under the sun. In their place came a more intense, more genuine look of terror and... grievance. "I... who am I?" He seemed not to understand what Shen Li was asking, repeating it blankly. Then, his beautiful peach-blossom eyes quickly filled with moisture. "I... who else could I be... Princess... I am Xiao Cheng..." As he spoke, he actually grabbed Shen Li’s hand in return, his movements carrying a desperate, humble craving. "Princess, why... why do you ask that? Is it... did I do something wrong again?" His tears fell without warning, landing on the back of Shen Li’s hand, scalding hot. "I... I know I'm useless, I'm not worthy of you... I know everything I do, in your eyes, is stupid and ridiculous..." "That time at the Treasure Pavilion, I... I just wanted to buy you a hairpin. I wanted... I wanted to do something to make you happy, but I'm useless. I couldn't even deal with a Minister's son, and I could only take out the golden medallion Father gave me to scare people..." "The Yanyu Pavilion... I... I wasn't there to seek pleasure! I swear!" He cried even harder, his voice choked with sobs. "I just heard people say it was the place with the most information in the capital. I wanted... I wanted to find out some news that would be useful to you. I wanted to help you... but I'm too stupid. I even had to set up a sand table just to talk to people, and in the end... in the end, I still messed things up and caused you to get hurt..." This account was a complete reversal of right and wrong, utterly absurd! Yet, coming from his mouth, paired with his tearful, heartbroken expression, it possessed a strange, compelling "rationality" that one couldn't help but believe. He attributed all his deep calculations to "stupid attempts to please." He explained all his conspiratorial layouts as "the desperate, incompetent struggles of a coward for the sake of his beloved." Shen Li felt so disgusted by this shameless "confession" that she almost vomited on the spot. She tried to pull her hand back, but he gripped it tightly. "Princess..." Seeing her silent, he cried even more miserably, even kneeling down, looking up with his handsome, tear-streaked face, and said in a tone that was almost pleading. "I just... I just love you too much..." "From the day Father bestowed the marriage, I knew that I, this useless wretch, was the luckiest person in the world. Being able to marry you is a blessing I earned over several lifetimes." "I know you look down on me, I know the whole world looks down on me. But what can I do? I've been like this since I was a child! I don't know martial arts, I don't understand strategy; the only thing I can do is... is to treat you well in my own clumsy, stupid way..." "You ask who I am? I am Xiao Cheng, a useless wretch who loves his princess deeply, yet is cowardly and incompetent, forever destined to hide behind you!" These words struck Shen Li’s heart hard. It didn't evoke emotion; it evoked overwhelming disgust and fury! She looked at the man kneeling on the ground, crying like a child, looking at his face filled with "sincerity" and "admiration," and a strong impulse surged in her heart. She wanted to pull out the broken arrow still embedded in her shoulder and stab it deep into his glib mouth, making him shut up forever! But she couldn't. His performance was flawless. Every word of his defense fit his "useless" persona perfectly. She could find no flaws. All her suspicions, all her interrogations, became pale and powerless in the face of this performance, which could only be described as masterful; they even began to feel like unreasonable harassment. Finally, Shen Li used all her strength to violently shake off his hand. "Get lost." She squeezed the words out through gritted teeth. Xiao Cheng stumbled from her shove and fell to the ground. He didn't get up, just stared at her blankly. Tears were still streaming down his face, but his expression had shifted from sorrow to a bewildered confusion, as if he couldn't understand what he had done wrong. Shen Li stopped looking at him, turned around, and returned to her tent. The moment the tent flap fell, she could even hear his suppressed, painful whimpering from behind her. With a "bang," she swept a teacup off the table inside the tent, sending it crashing to the floor! Her chest heaved violently, pulling at the wound on her shoulder and sending waves of tearing pain through her, but this physical pain was nothing compared to the stifling frustration and fury in her heart! Liar! This man was a complete and utter liar! Yet, she was utterly helpless against him! - Ever since that day, it was as if Xiao Cheng’s heart had been completely shattered by that single word, "get lost," from Shen Li. He no longer tried to get close to her, locking himself in the carriage all day, washing his face with tears. Then, he fell "ill." A sudden, "serious illness." First, it was a persistent high fever and delirium, followed by violent, soul-wrenching coughing that sounded as if he were trying to cough up his very heart, liver, spleen, and lungs. The accompanying military physician diagnosed that the Prince was suffering from excessive worry, compounded by the exhaustion of travel and the intrusion of cold into his body, which had damaged his foundation. Thus, this Seventh Prince became a complete medicine-guzzler. At every meal, he had to drink large bowls of bitter decoctions. The carriage was filled with a heavy, medicinal scent all day long. Occasionally, when the curtain was lifted, one would see him wrapped in thick fur blankets, his complexion sallow, looking weak enough to breathe his last at any moment. With him ill, the burden of the entire caravan naturally fell squarely onto Shen Li’s shoulders alone. - Her injuries were, in fact, far more severe than his. Although the arrow poison had been neutralized, the wound that had pierced her shoulder blade continued to torment her day and night. Every time she raised her arm or turned her body, a piercing, bone-deep pain would shoot through her. But she could not fall. She was the only one left in this group who could take charge. She became the commander in every sense of the word. Every day before dawn, she would rise, enduring the pain, to inspect the camp. She had to personally review the maps sent back by scouts, plan the daily route, and avoid bandits and dangerous terrain. She had to personally coordinate personnel, arranging the defensive duties for the three hundred Shen family soldiers and the mysterious Black Armor Army to ensure the absolute safety of the caravan and the supplies. She even had to personally interrogate the spies captured along the way, prying out any useful information about Cangbei from them. She processed everything at high speed, tirelessly. At night, when everyone else had fallen asleep, she would drag her exhausted body in front of the maps, repeatedly simulating scenarios and studying the unfamiliar and dangerous land they were about to enter. No one knew that she would be drenched in cold sweat every night because her wound was inflamed. Several times, she had to grit her teeth and use a dagger to cut away the rotting flesh herself before applying the medicinal powder. - All of this was seen by the person in the carriage. Of course, not with his own eyes. Deep in the night. Xuan Yi, the commander of the Black Armor Army, appeared outside Xiao Cheng’s carriage like a phantom, silent and still. He knelt on one knee and reported the day's situation in a voice only he could hear. "Master, we traveled 120 miles today. No enemy activity." "The Princess has readjusted the marching formation, placing the supply wagons in the center, with the three hundred Shen family soldiers guarding both sides. My fifty men are acting as vanguard scouts, and fifty are bringing up the rear. The formation... is flawless." "In the afternoon, the Princess personally interrogated three spies, asking entirely about the troop deployments of the Ma family and the Black Wind Stronghold in Cangbei." A suppressed cough came from inside the carriage. Immediately, a weak yet incredibly steady voice replied. "How is... her injury?" "The physician says the Princess's wound is not healing well, and she developed a high fever again tonight. She... refused the physician's treatment." A long silence fell inside the carriage. It lasted so long that Xuan Yi thought his master had fallen asleep, before the voice spoke again, carrying a trace of imperceptible... fatigue. "Pass the order to slow the marching speed." "Also, find a way to mix that 'Snow Jade Ginseng' from my private vault into her medicine." "...Yes." Xuan Yi acknowledged the order, then hesitated. "Master, your health..." "I won't die." The voice returned to its usual coldness. "Do as I say." Xuan Yi dared not say more. His figure flickered and vanished into the night. - Inside the carriage, Xiao Cheng slowly opened his eyes. In the darkness, his eyes were startlingly bright. Where was there any sign of illness? He lifted a corner of the curtain, his gaze piercing through the heavy night and landing precisely on the only tent in the distance that was still lit. He could imagine that woman, right now, forcing herself to stay upright, sitting before the map with furrowed brows, racking her brains for the future of this group. Her resilience, her tenacity, and her innate, exceptional military talent were being displayed to the fullest in this predicament he had deliberately created. She was like a precious blade hidden in a scabbard; only in harsh environments could she reveal her edge. And he was the one who would personally hone her to be sharper, and more... invincible. A complex smile curled the corner of Xiao Cheng’s mouth. The more you hate me now, the more you want me dead. The more you will rely on me in the future, the more you will be unable to leave me. Shen Li, my Princess. Our game has only just begun. On the other side, Shen Li sneezed. She rubbed her throbbing forehead, assuming the night wind was just too cold. She glanced out the window at Xiao Cheng’s carriage; it was pitch black and unusually quiet. Occasionally, she could hear one or two deliberately suppressed coughs, asserting the owner's presence. A flash of undisguised contempt and a cold sneer crossed Shen Li’s eyes. Useless. She scoffed coldly in her heart. You had better stay this useless for the rest of your life!

chapters.title: The Hongmen Banquet
chapters.content:
The caravan traveled through the wind and sand for nearly a month.

When the silhouette of the city, built entirely of gray-brown boulders at the edge of the wasteland, first appeared on the horizon, even the iron-willed Shen family soldiers erupted into a suppressed cheer.

Cangbei City.

They had finally arrived.

But the closer they got, the weaker that suppressed cheering became, eventually fading into a heavy silence.

The city walls were tall but dilapidated. The massive stones were covered in the marks of wind and frost erosion. On the battlements, a sparse number of soldiers in mismatched leather armor stood about. Their posture was crooked, their spears rusty; they looked less like soldiers and more like a group of bandits who had seized the mountain.

And the most chilling sight was the massive, iron-clad city gate, which remained tightly shut.

There were no flags, no honor guards above the gate.

Welcoming this royal exile party was nothing but dead silence and the undisguised, scrutinizing, and provocative gazes of those on the wall.

Scouts had long since delivered the news of the Prince’s arrival to the city. By regulation, local officials should have come out ten miles to kneel and welcome the royal carriage.

But now, let alone officials, there wasn't even anyone to open the gate.

"This is outrageous!" The captain of the personal guard, Uncle Zhang, rode up to Shen Li, his face livid with anger. "These sons of bitches! How dare they slight the royal carriage! My Lady, I request to lead a team to call them out!"

Shen Li did not speak.

She pulled on the reins and looked up at the gatehouse.

There, she saw that a grand armchair covered in tiger skin had appeared. A middle-aged man with a bloated, fleshy face sat on it like a king, twirling two walnuts in his hand, looking down at them from above with undisguised contempt.

Behind the man stood a row of arrogant-looking retainers; clearly, he was the master of this place.

"Princess, that man is Ma Wanshan," a guard who had studied intelligence on Cangbei back in the capital whispered in Shen Li’s ear. "The most powerful tycoon in Cangbei. It is said that he controls half of the grain and salt-iron trade in Cangbei. Eighty percent of the garrison in the city are his private soldiers."

Shen Li narrowed her eyes slightly.

Quite the show of force.

Just then, Ma Wanshan on the gatehouse seemed to feel he had kept them waiting long enough. He slowly stood up, walked to the edge of the wall, and shouted in a voice loud enough for the entire caravan to hear:

"Are those the Seventh Prince and Princess from the capital down there?"

His voice carried an unpleasant, oily tone.

"Here in Cangbei, it’s a poor and treacherous place; we don't have so many tedious rituals. We only recognize fists and only respect the strong!"

"I heard the Seventh Prince was quite the figure in the capital. Since you've come to our Cangbei, you must show us a trick or two to open the eyes of us rough folk, right?"

"Otherwise, my brothers won't be convinced, and I’m afraid this city gate won't be easy to open!"

"Hahahahaha!"

As soon as he finished speaking, an unbridled roar of laughter erupted from the entire city wall.

These words were no longer a provocation; they were a naked humiliation!

"Too much!"

"Let's fight them!"

The three hundred Shen family soldiers were incensed, the sound of swords being drawn ringing out in unison. They were the elite under the Duke of Zhenguo; when had they ever suffered such a great insult!

Just at this tense moment.

"Wuu..."

A very faint, tearful whimper drifted out from the most luxurious carriage.

Immediately following it was Xiao Cheng’s suppressed whisper, filled with deep terror.

"Princess... are they... are they bad people? Should we... should we just go back... I'm scared..."

Veins bulged on Shen Li’s forehead.

She violently turned her horse around, her eyes, burning with rage, fixed on that tightly closed curtain.

Go back?

Do you think this is a vegetable market in the suburbs of the capital, where you can come and go as you please!

The fury in her heart reached its peak at this moment.

She was not angry at Ma Wanshan, nor at the harassment from these local thugs. On the battlefield, she had seen scenes a hundred times more perilous than this.

She was angry at the useless man behind her—the one who could only cry, only hide, and only push her into the eye of the storm!

A violent impulse to destroy everything surged within her.

Shen Li took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the urge to draw her blade and hack that carriage to pieces.

She didn't spare the carriage another glance and swung down from her horse.

With a sharp "clang," she drew a twelve-foot-long spear made entirely of refined steel, tipped with a dragon-gall silver point, from beside her saddle.

She wore no helmet, only a set of black combat gear, her long hair tied high, whipping in the wind. Alone, with a single spear, she walked step by step toward Cangbei City, which crouched like a giant beast.

With every step she took, the Shen Army behind her grew quieter.

When she reached a point a hundred paces from the city gate, it was as if she were the only person left in the entire world.

The jeering from the city walls gradually ceased.

All eyes were fixed on that seemingly slender, yet straight-as-a-pine figure.

Ma Wanshan looked at the woman walking toward him alone. A flash of surprise crossed his eyes, quickly replaced by a more intense greed and interest.

"What a fine, spirited mare! It wouldn't be bad if she could bear children for my Ma family!" He licked his thick lips and signaled to the three fierce henchmen beside him.

"Go down and entertain her. Remember, don't ruin her face."

Those three henchmen were desperate criminals whom Ma Wanshan had paid handsomely to keep; every one of them had blood on their hands. They grinned hideously, accepted the order, and sprinted down the stairs on the side of the city wall.

A moment later, the drawbridge slowly lowered. The three burly men stood in a triangular formation, wielding heavy weapons, and blocked Shen Li’s path.

"Little lady, I advise you to surrender obediently and follow our Master Ma. We'll ensure you live in luxury!" the scarred man in the lead said with a lecherous grin.

Shen Li did not speak.

She simply raised the long spear in her hand slowly.

Seeing her silence, the scarred man assumed she was afraid. His courage bolstered, he let out a roar, swung his mountain-splitting axe, and hacked straight at Shen Li’s head!

The axe was heavy and powerful, whistling through the air. If an ordinary person were hit, their bones would surely shatter!

However, Shen Li did not move an inch.

Just as the axe blade was about to touch the tips of her hair, she moved.

No one saw how she struck.

There was only a crisp "ding!"

The scarred man’s body suddenly stiffened, the hideous grin still frozen on his face. He looked down at his chest in disbelief.

Before anyone knew it, the tip of the silver spear had pierced through his prized breastplate, leaving a tiny, inconspicuous hole.

No blood flowed out.

Because the spear was too fast.

So fast that even the blood couldn't react in time.

"Thud!"

The burly man’s massive body fell straight backward, kicking up a cloud of dust.

One strike.

Just one strike.

The remaining two henchmen’s flippancy vanished instantly, replaced by unprecedented gravity! They exchanged a glance, let out a simultaneous roar, and charged from left and right, brandishing a mace and an iron chain!

Shen Li flicked her wrist, and the long spear traced a graceful arc in the air, the shaft bending into an astonishing curve with incredible flexibility.

"Clang! Clang!"

Two loud bangs!

The seemingly flexible spear struck the mace and the iron chain with pinpoint precision at the same time!

The two henchmen felt a massive force surge from their weapons. Their palms split open instantly, and their weapons flew from their hands uncontrollably, rebounding with even greater speed to smash heavily into their own chests!

"Pfft!"

Both men spat out a mist of blood and flew several yards away. By the time they hit the ground, they were barely breathing.

Still one strike.

Within three moves, three fierce henchmen were dead or severely wounded.

The battlefield fell into a dead silence.

Whether it was Ma Wanshan’s private soldiers on the wall or the Shen Army outside the city, everyone was too stunned to speak by this overwhelming, crushing display of power.

Shen Li stood with her spear retracted, the tip pointing diagonally at the ground. A single drop of blood slid slowly down the smooth blade and dripped into the dust.

She slowly raised her head, her cold eyes fixed on the bloodless, fat man on the city wall.

She said nothing.

But her gaze said it all.

Ma Wanshan felt a chill run through his entire body; his hands, which were busy rolling walnuts, were trembling slightly.

He finally understood what kind of existence he had provoked.

That was no spirited mare; that was a... tigress!

Shen Li turned her spear point toward the tightly shut city gate and finally spoke.

Her voice was not loud, but it reached everyone’s ears clearly.

"Open the gate."

The two words carried the weight of a thousand tons.

Ma Wanshan’s legs went weak, and he could barely stand. He instinctively took a step back and roared at the terrified city guard beside him, his voice trembling with feigned ferocity:

"Open... open the gate! Open it quickly!"

The heavy city gate let out a creaking sound and slowly swung inward.

Shen Li did not enter immediately.

She carried her spear, turned around, and walked back to her troops step by step.

The three hundred Shen soldiers looked at their returning commander, at the long spear still dripping with blood, and a fanatical worship erupted in all their eyes!

This was their General!

No words needed, no nonsense required!

Using the most direct force to win everyone’s respect!

The convoy slowly drove into Cangbei City.

As they passed the Prince's carriage, Shen Li did not pause for a second.

However, the carriage curtain was quietly lifted by a hand.

Xiao Cheng poked half his head out, looking at the back of the woman who was radiating such murderous intent, like a Valkyrie. The "terrified" expression on his face had not yet fully faded.

He quietly, cautiously, gave a thumbs-up to her back.

In a voice only he could hear, he sighed with heartfelt admiration:

"Your Highness, you are mighty!"

chapters.title: What’s the Point of Being a Prince If You Can’t Even Get a Full Meal!
chapters.content:
The Seventh Prince’s Mansion in Cangbei City was less of a mansion and more of a haunted house that had been abandoned for years.

Most of the courtyard walls had collapsed, revealing dark, jagged gaps. Weeds grew taller than a person, swaying in the howling north wind with a "rustling" sound. The vermilion paint on the main gate had long since peeled away, exposing the rotting wood beneath. A few crows stood on the lintel, letting out hoarse, unpleasant cries.

Pushing the door open, a smell of decay rushed to meet them. Half of the rockery in the courtyard had toppled over, the pond had long since dried up, and the cracked bottom was filled with withered branches and dead leaves. The so-called halls were nothing more than a few dilapidated rooms with drafts blowing in from all sides; the paper on the windows was tattered, and the cold wind whistling through them sounded like wailing.

This was the residence the Emperor had bestowed upon his son.

The three hundred Shen soldiers and the one hundred mysterious Black Armor soldiers were now stationed in these ruins. They silently cleared the weeds and patched the holes, their faces devoid of any expression.

The shock of the Princess’s earth-shattering three moves at the city gate had long since been dispelled by the despairing poverty before them.

They were elite soldiers who had fought a hundred battles; they did not fear death, but they could not endure hunger.

The dry rations brought from the capital had been exhausted during the month-long trek. And this city seemed even poorer than they had imagined.

In this oppressive atmosphere, the few local officials of Cangbei City, led by a pale, beardless, and thin "Prefect," came to "pay their respects" to their new master.

The front hall was actually just a slightly larger, less drafty shack.

Shen Li, in full military uniform, sat in the main seat with her arms crossed, her face expressionless. The wound on her shoulder had not yet healed, and every breath brought a faint, stinging pain, which was nothing compared to the irritation in her heart.

As soon as the officials entered, they flopped onto their knees and began to wail and howl.

"Your Highness, Princess! This humble official... this humble official is guilty!"

The Prefect in the lead kowtowed while crying: "It is not that we dared to neglect your Highness, but truly... truly there is no grain left in the city!"

"There was a great drought in Cangbei this year, and not a single grain was harvested. The people can only survive by gnawing on tree bark and eating grass roots. We... we haven't had a full meal in days. We are truly... truly powerless to host a welcoming banquet. We hope the Prince and Princess will forgive us!"

As he spoke, he actually pulled a rock-hard, black-flour bun—who knows how old it was—from his sleeve, held it high, and wept bitterly.

"Your Highness, look! This is this humble official’s ration for today! We... we are truly poor!"

This performance could not have been more exquisite.

Uncle Zhang, standing behind Shen Li, was so angry that his fists clenched.

He could see at a glance that although these men wore patched official robes, they were all ruddy-faced and full of vigor; there was no sign of starvation about them.

This was clearly another attempt to intimidate them!

Shen Li said nothing; she just looked coldly at these clowns. She wanted to see how her "good husband" would deal with this.

"Waaa... wah—!"

An earth-shattering howl suddenly erupted from behind the screen.

Xiao Cheng rushed out from a dilapidated room behind them. He had completely shed his sickly appearance from the road; he now looked "full of spirit," though all that energy was being poured into his wailing.

He sat on the floor, kicking his legs, pounding his chest, and crying a hundred times more miserably than the Prefect.

"No food?!"

"Not even a full meal?! Then why did I come here! What’s the point of me being a Prince!"

He cried while wiping away non-existent tears with his sleeves, issuing a heart-wrenching accusation at the officials who were now dumbfounded.

"I don't care! I don't care!"

"When I was in the capital, I ate fragrant rice newly offered from the south every day, and drank soup stewed with Tianshan snow lotus! Even for rinsing my mouth, I used bird's nest stewed with official-grade swallow's nests!"

"You... you are actually telling me now that you don't even have enough to eat? Are you trying to starve me to death? You bunch of unruly commoners! You corrupt officials!"

As he cursed, he rolled around on the floor, looking exactly like a three-year-old child who couldn't get his candy.

The entire front hall fell into a deathly silence.

The officials, kneeling on the ground, stared in stunned silence at the Prince rolling on the floor. They forgot to even feign sorrow, their faces left with nothing but shock and disdain.

They had anticipated many scenarios.

They had expected this new Prince to be thunderously angry, to draw his sword and kill.

But they had never imagined he would... throw a tantrum.

Shen Li’s face turned livid.

She felt a surge of blood rush to her head, causing black spots to dance before her eyes.

Disgraceful!

It was fucking disgraceful!

Shen Li had been on the battlefield for ten years; what hadn't she seen? Yet today, she truly wanted to find a crack in the ground to crawl into!

"Enough!"

Unable to bear it any longer, she let out a furious roar, stepped forward, and kicked Xiao Cheng—who was still rolling on the floor—right in the backside!

She put her full strength into that kick.

Xiao Cheng let out an "Awoo," and like a rubber ball, he was sent rolling a long way, only stopping when he slammed into a pillar.

He didn't get up. He just sprawled on the floor, hugging the pillar, and continued to wail, "Woooo... my bird's nest... my delicacies... woooo..."

Shen Li didn't even glance at him; she was afraid that if she looked again, she wouldn't be able to stop herself from drawing her blade and hacking this piece of trash to death.

She swept a cold gaze over the officials kneeling on the floor.

"Where is the official granary in the city?"

The Governor trembled under her gaze and instinctively replied, "It's... it's in the west of the city..."

"Lead the way."

Shen Li dropped the two words coldly and turned to leave.

"Uncle Zhang! Gather fifty men and come with me!"

"Yes!"

Uncle Zhang had been holding back a belly full of rage. Now that he had his orders, he felt a surge of energy. He immediately rounded up the men and followed closely behind Shen Li, looking murderous as they escorted the trembling officials straight toward the west-side granary.

The gate of the granary was kicked open.

However, the scene inside left everyone stunned.

The massive warehouse was completely empty, not even a single grain of rice remained. Thick dust covered the floor, and several large rats scurried across the empty grain racks.

The granary was truly empty!

"Your... Your Highness, please spare me!" The Governor was so terrified he lost all composure, kneeling on the ground and kowtowing frantically. "This official... everything this official said is true! The grain in the city really... really was all bought up by the Ma family!"

"The Ma family?" Shen Li’s eyes sharpened.

"Yes... it's Master Ma, Ma Wanshan..." the Governor said, trembling. "He said... he said he saw that you and the Prince had traveled from afar and couldn't bear to see you worry about provisions, so... so he bought up all the grain in the city in advance, intending... intending to offer it to the Prince..."

Offer?

Shen Li sneered.

I’m afraid he wants to use the grain to choke the life out of her army!

Sure enough, less than half an hour later, the Ma family sent someone to deliver their "greetings."

The man who arrived was arrogant and haughty, saying that Master Ma was sympathetic to the Imperial army and was willing to sell a batch of grain to help the Princess out of her immediate predicament.

The only catch was that the price was... ten times the price of rice in the capital!

"They’ve gone too far!" Uncle Zhang smashed his fist against the wall in anger. "Young Miss! Let's fight them! We'll storm the Ma residence and seize their granary!"

"No," Shen Li shook her head.

They had just arrived and their foundation was not yet stable. The Ma family had operated in Cangbei for many years, and their eyes and ears—and private soldiers—were everywhere in the city. If they acted rashly, they would only fall into the quagmire of street fighting and be worn down to death.

More importantly, the fact remained that the army was out of food.

Her four hundred elite soldiers could fight to the death for her, but they could not fight to the death on empty stomachs.

Stabilizing the morale of the army was the most important thing right now.

"Uncle Zhang," Shen Li’s voice carried a hint of exhaustion, "go and bring out all the private assets I brought with me."

"...Young Miss, you cannot!" Uncle Zhang was horrified. "That is your dowry! It was given to you by the Old Duke for your own security!"

"Carry out the order." Shen Li’s tone allowed no room for argument.

In the end, with red-rimmed eyes, Uncle Zhang handed over several large chests of gold and jewelry to the Ma family in exchange for just enough grain to keep the army fed for a few days.

When the steaming hot meat porridge was distributed to every soldier, the morale of the entire camp finally stabilized.

Shen Li held a bowl of porridge, but she had no appetite at all.

She looked at her empty luggage, and for the first time, she felt that emotion known as "powerlessness."

She didn't fear charging into battle, nor did she fear mountains of knives or seas of fire.

But this feeling of being constrained at every turn, of being manipulated by schemes and tricks, made her feel incredibly stifled.

Just then, a "heaven-shaking" wail erupted from that dilapidated room again.

"I won't drink it! I won't drink this!"

"How is this any different from pig slop?! I want bird's nest porridge! I want to rinse my mouth with bird's nest! Woooo..."

Shen Li held the bowl of steaming meat porridge, listening to the man inside throwing a tantrum over a bowl of non-existent bird's nest. She stood in the cold wind, motionless for a long time.

She suddenly felt that the wind and snow of Cangbei... didn't seem so cold after all.

What truly made her feel cold was this boundless, endless despair.

chapters.title: Cutting Off Water and Grain? Are You Trying to Rebel!
chapters.content:
Relying on the high-priced grain bought with Shen Li’s dowry, the army in the Prince’s residence finally escaped the immediate crisis of running out of food.

The gloom that had hung over everyone’s hearts for days seemed to have been dispelled somewhat by that pot of steaming meat porridge. The soldiers gulped down the hard-won food, and color began to return to their faces.

But this brief peace was as fragile as a layer of window paper.

Three days later, that paper was mercilessly pierced.

"It’s bad! Your Highness!"

A soldier responsible for sentry duty scrambled into the "council hall"—a room that barely kept out the wind and rain—his face full of terror.

"The... the Yinma River outside the city has run dry!"

"What?!"

Shen Li, who was discussing defense with Uncle Zhang and the others, stood up abruptly.

The Yinma River was the only surface water source in Cangbei City. The drinking water for the entire city’s military and civilians relied on this river, which flowed down from the snow-capped Western Mountains.

Run dry? How could that be! It was early summer, the time when melting ice and snow should make the river at its most abundant!

Shen Li immediately led her men to the riverbank.

The sight before them made everyone gasp.

The riverbed, which had once surged with endless water, now had only a thin line of water struggling to survive on the parched ground. In the murky mud, dead fish with white bellies floated, emitting a foul stench.

Within half a day, even that thin line of water disappeared completely.

The Yinma River had truly run dry.

Panic, like a plague, swept through the entire city of Cangbei in an instant.

The commoners, carrying wooden buckets, swarmed like madmen toward the few half-dry wells in the city, fighting until they were bloodied just to scramble for a spoonful of muddy water.

And the four hundred elites in the Prince’s residence were in complete chaos.

"There’s no water to drink! We’re all going to die of thirst here!"

"In this godforsaken place, we can't even get a drink of water, what's the point of fighting!"

"I’m done! I’m going back to the capital! If I’m going to die, I’ll die somewhere with water!"

The morale of the army began to waver.

Even the most loyal Shen family soldiers could not remain calm in the face of death. Food could be rationed, but water could not be cut off for even a single day.

"Shut your mouths, all of you!" Uncle Zhang drew his sword, his face livid as he suppressed the restless soldiers. "Whoever dares to spread rumors and disrupt the morale of the army again, I will kill without mercy!"

His authority temporarily suppressed the situation. But those faces, twisted by thirst and fear, were like explosives waiting to be detonated at any moment.

Shen Li stood on the riverbank, looking at the cracked riverbed, her phoenix eyes filled with cold murderous intent.

A drought? The riverbed dried up?

Nonsense!

She clearly saw that upstream, someone had used giant rocks and mud to build a crude but effective dam, diverting the river in another direction.

This was the Ma family’s handiwork.

After the grain, it was the water supply.

This local tyrant wanted to use this "boiling a frog in warm water" method to trap them to death and force them out of Cangbei!

Sure enough, not long after, the Ma family’s steward arrived at the Prince’s residence in a swaggering manner.

He didn't mention the word "water," but with a face full of "sorrow," he told Shen Li that rumors were spreading throughout the city that the new Prince and Princess had offended the River God who protected Cangbei, and that the Dragon King was angry and had taken the water away.

"Your Highness," the steward sighed hypocritically, "Master Ma is also concerned about the people of the city. He says that the person who tied the bell must be the one to untie it. Perhaps... perhaps if the people who angered the Dragon King leave, the river water will return on its own?"

These words, seemingly just rumors, were actually an ultimatum.

Either get out, or die of thirst.

"Get out!" Uncle Zhang was so angry he kicked the steward out the door.

But while the man could be driven away, the crisis could not be resolved.

The army’s water skins were already hitting the bottom.

That afternoon, the first real mutiny broke out in the army.

Dozens of soldiers surrounded the last few barrels of stored water and clashed violently with the guards.

"Let us drink water!"

"If we don't drink water, we’re going to die!"

"Why can you drink it, but we can't!"

The situation spiraled out of control; swords were drawn, and blood was spilled.

When Shen Li arrived, several wounded soldiers were already lying on the ground. She didn't waste a single word; she acted directly, with thunderous force, breaking the limbs of the soldiers who had led the riot on the spot.

The bloody suppression temporarily stabilized the situation.

But Shen Li knew this was only the beginning.

People could be killed, but they could not be "thirsted" to death. If this continued, her army would collapse from within long before the Ma family even had to lift a finger.

What to do?

Did she really have to do as Uncle Zhang said—storm the Ma residence and bathe Cangbei in blood?

She gripped the hilt of her sword, her knuckles turning white from the pressure.

Just then, the door of that dilapidated room, which had been kept tightly shut for days, creaked open.

Xiao Cheng walked out.

He did not cry, nor did he make a scene. He changed into a clean Confucian robe, his face even wearing a strange expression that blended compassion for the world with solemnity.
